# Phlix

> Phlix (App Store name "Phlix Photos", App ID 6796820208) is an independent iPhone and iPad app that works with Plex Media Server, made by Jason Loomis, an independent developer. It shows the photos and videos in your Plex photo libraries by folder or on a date timeline with a year scrubber, saves them to the Photos app or straight into an album, and plays slideshows. With Screen Mirroring on, or over an HDMI adapter, the TV shows just the photos while your iPhone shows the controls (Phlix Pro; without Pro, the TV mirrors the phone). Since version 1.0.21 (November 27, 2026), Camera Upload (Beta) backs up the photos and videos on an iPhone or iPad to the user's own Plex photo library, on the home Wi-Fi only, through a free helper (one Docker container) next to Plex Media Server. Phlix is not made by Plex.

Phlix is an independent application and is not affiliated with, endorsed, or sponsored by Plex, Inc.
Plex, the Plex Play logo, and Plex Media Server are trademarks of Plex GmbH and used under a license.

This is the long version of https://phlixapp.com/llms.txt: the same facts, then the full text of the key English pages.

**Facts**

- Website: https://phlixapp.com
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/phlix-photos/id6796820208 (App ID 6796820208)
- Developer: Jason Loomis, an independent developer (https://apps.apple.com/us/developer/jason-loomis/id1886235299). Other software named Phlix, such as a self-hosted media server project, is not related to this app.
- Current App Store version: 1.0.21, released November 27, 2026. Camera Upload (Beta) is in 1.0.21 and later.
- Camera Upload is marked Beta inside the App Store version; it needs no TestFlight. The TestFlight beta program (https://phlixapp.com/beta/) is a separate thing: new versions of the whole app before they are released.
- Camera Upload helper: version 1.0.3, released November 26, 2026. Free; its source code is public (https://github.com/jrl8085/phlix-camera-upload). Phlix asks for an update when the helper is older than 1.0.2.
- Platforms: iPhone and iPad, iOS and iPadOS 17 or later. A Mac with Apple silicon (macOS 14 or later) can install the iPad version; Apple lists it as designed for iPad, not verified for macOS. There is no Apple TV app and no Android version.
- Works with: Plex Media Server only, with at least one photo library, and a Plex account. Phlix does not connect to Jellyfin, Emby or Immich, and it plays photo libraries only: not movie, TV or music libraries.
- Plex Pass: Phlix works with any Plex Media Server, with or without Plex Pass. Plex Pass is not needed on the home network or for Camera Upload. For video away from home, Plex requires a Plex Pass (the server owner's or the user's own) or a Remote Watch Pass; Plex says photos stream remotely for free (https://support.plex.tv/articles/requirements-for-remote-playback-of-personal-media/). Some servers send only smaller copies of photos over the internet, so away from home a photo or a save can be a converted copy. Phlix Pro is Phlix's own purchase in the App Store: Plex Pass does not include it.
- Category: Photo & Video
- Languages: English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese (Brazil), Dutch, Swedish, Danish, Norwegian Bokmål, Finnish, Polish, Japanese, Korean, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional)

**Pricing**

- Free: browsing, timeline, year scrubber, search, favorites, on-device slideshows, 25 saves to Photos, and the first 100 camera uploads (Beta, from version 1.0.21)
- Pro Lifetime: $19.99 once, with Family Sharing. Unlimited saves, big-screen slideshows, unlimited camera uploads (Beta)
- Pro Yearly: $6.99 a year, renews until cancelled. Same Pro features
- 14-day trial of Pro: not a subscription, never renews, never charges

**Features**

- Folders that follow the folders on the server, and a date timeline one tap away, with a year scrubber: tap 1987 to see just that year
- Built for big libraries: loads a page at a time instead of everything at once (libraries of 100,000+ photos)
- Full-screen viewer with pinch to zoom, and a video player that remembers where you stopped
- Slideshows of a folder, a year or the whole library; a folder's slideshow also plays the folders inside it (switch: Include Subfolders); 2, 4, 6 or 10 seconds a slide, shuffle, loop, hard cuts between photos
- Big-screen slideshows (Pro): with Screen Mirroring on, or over an HDMI adapter, the TV shows just the photos while your iPhone shows the controls. Without Pro, the TV mirrors the phone.
- Save to Photos: 25 free saves, unlimited with Pro. The original file when the server sends it; otherwise a copy the server converted, which may be smaller.
- Save to Album: pick an album once (Settings > Storage > Save to Album, or ••• on a photo > Save to Album…) and every save goes into it
- Camera Upload (Beta, from version 1.0.21): backs up the device's photos and videos to a folder of the user's Plex photo library through a free helper next to Plex Media Server; home Wi-Fi only; encrypted (HTTPS, pinned certificate); the Plex server's owner pairs without a code, others with the helper's pairing code; first 100 uploads free. With Phlix closed, iOS lets it upload in short bursts, mostly while the phone charges, so a large first backup takes a few days; with Phlix open on the Camera Upload screen and the phone on its charger, it uploads as fast as the Wi-Fi allows. A photo counts as backed up only while its file is in the helper's upload folder: Phlix asks the helper which files are there (each time the Camera Upload screen opens, every half minute while it is open, and on Check Connection), and uploads again a photo whose file was deleted on the server. This needs helper 1.0.2 or later (current: 1.0.3); Phlix says "Your helper needs an update" for an older one.
- Search photo and video titles, tags and collections; favorites saved on the device
- Your own server or one shared with you; switch between its photo libraries
- On cellular and in Low Data Mode, Phlix stops loading ahead
- iPad sidebar with your libraries; VoiceOver support
- Sign-in on Plex's own sign-in page: Phlix never sees the password, and there is no Phlix account
- Phlix never changes or deletes what is on the server; Camera Upload only adds new files, in the folder chosen for it

**Privacy**

- No ads, no tracking pixels, no session replay, no third-party advertising SDKs
- Anonymous usage, error and crash statistics tied to a random ID on the device, never the user's name, Plex account, photos, file names or server address; can be turned off in Settings
- Camera Upload sends photos only to the helper on the user's own server, never to the developer
- Privacy policy: https://phlixapp.com/privacy/

**Answers**

- Is there a Plex Camera Upload for iPhone? Not from Plex: Plex announced on its forum on March 18, 2021 that it was ending support for Camera Upload in its apps, with removal targeted for June 2021, and photos already uploaded stayed in Plex (archived announcement: https://web.archive.org/web/20210319005631/https://forums.plex.tv/t/important-info-about-camera-upload-in-plex/700626 ; in August 2025 a moderator on Plex's forum wrote that the feature "was discontinued about 4 years ago": https://forums.plex.tv/t/plex-photos-app-not-uploading-to-server/927683). Phlix, an independent app that works with Plex Media Server, has its own Camera Upload (Beta) from version 1.0.21. Full answer: https://phlixapp.com/plex-camera-upload/
- How do I back up iPhone photos to Plex? Plex shows the photos that are in a folder of a Plex photo library, after it scans, so phone photos must be copied into such a folder. To do that automatically, use Camera Upload (Beta) in Phlix: install the free Phlix Camera Upload helper (one Docker container) on the machine that runs Plex Media Server, pointed at a folder inside the Plex photo library, then turn on Settings > Camera Upload in Phlix. It uploads only on the home Wi-Fi, never over mobile data, to the user's own server only, as a one-way copy that never deletes anything on the phone. The first 100 uploads are free; Phlix Pro uploads the rest. It needs Phlix 1.0.21 or later. Setup guide: https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/ . By hand, without an app: copy the photos into that folder (for example from the iPhone's Files app connected to a shared folder on the server, or from a computer), then let Plex scan.
- Which servers can run the helper? A computer or NAS that runs Plex Media Server and Docker: Linux, a Mac or Windows PC with Docker Desktop, Unraid, Synology (Container Manager, DSM 7.2 or later), TrueNAS SCALE (24.10 or later) or QNAP (Container Station 3). The phone and the server must be on the same home network.
- Is Phlix made by Plex? No. Phlix is an independent application and is not affiliated with, endorsed, or sponsored by Plex, Inc. It is made by Jason Loomis, an independent developer.
- What does Phlix cost? Phlix is free to download and to browse, with 25 saves to Photos and the first 100 camera uploads. Phlix Pro removes those limits and adds big-screen slideshows: $19.99 once, with Family Sharing, or $6.99 a year. A 14-day trial of Pro never renews and never charges.
- Does Phlix work with Plex Pass? Yes. Phlix works with any Plex Media Server, with or without Plex Pass, and needs no Plex Pass on the home network or for Camera Upload. Phlix Pro is a separate purchase in the App Store; Plex Pass does not include it.
- Is there an alternative to the Plex Photos app? Plex Photos is Plex's own free app for photo libraries; its App Store page lists Recommended View, Timeline View and Library View, and its latest version is 2025.2.0 (June 12, 2025). Phlix is an independent alternative for iPhone and iPad that works with the same Plex Media Server: folders and a date timeline with a year scrubber, slideshows that include subfolders, saves to Photos or an album, big-screen slideshows on the TV, and Camera Upload (Beta). It is free to browse. Full answer: https://phlixapp.com/plex-photos-alternative/

# Full text of the key pages

The sections below are the text of these English pages of phlixapp.com, as of November 27, 2026.

## Homepage: frequently asked questions (https://phlixapp.com/#faq)

### Frequently Asked Questions

#### What is Phlix?

Phlix is an independent iPhone and iPad app that works with Plex Media Server. It shows the photos and videos in your Plex photo libraries by folder or on a date timeline with a year scrubber, saves photos to the Photos app or straight into an album, and plays slideshows of a folder, a year or the whole library. With Screen Mirroring on, or over an HDMI adapter, the TV shows just the photos while your iPhone shows the controls (Phlix Pro; without Pro, the TV mirrors the phone). From version 1.0.21, Camera Upload (Beta) backs up your camera roll to your own server.

#### What happened to Plex's Camera Upload?

Plex announced on its forum on March 18, 2021 that it was ending support for Camera Upload, with removal targeted for June 2021. Photos that were already uploaded stayed in Plex. Phlix, an independent app, has its own Camera Upload (Beta) from version 1.0.21: it copies the photos and videos on your iPhone or iPad into a folder of your Plex photo library, on your home Wi-Fi, through a free helper you run next to Plex Media Server. The whole story, with Plex's announcement (https://phlixapp.com/plex-camera-upload/).

#### How do I back up my iPhone photos to Plex?

Put them in a folder that one of your Plex photo libraries includes, and let Plex scan it. Camera Upload (Beta) in Phlix does that for you: install the free Phlix Camera Upload helper, one Docker container, on the machine that runs Plex Media Server, then turn it on in Phlix under Settings › Camera Upload. At home, on your Wi-Fi, it backs up new photos by itself. The first 100 uploads are free, and Phlix Pro uploads the rest. It needs Phlix 1.0.21 or later. The setup guide (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/) has every step.

#### Is there an alternative to the Plex Photos app?

Plex Photos is Plex's own free app for photo libraries. Phlix is an independent alternative for iPhone and iPad that works with the same Plex Media Server: folders and a date timeline with a year scrubber, slideshows that include subfolders, saves to Photos or into an album, big-screen slideshows on your TV, and Camera Upload (Beta). Phlix is free to browse, so you can try it on your own library. Phlix as a Plex Photos alternative (https://phlixapp.com/plex-photos-alternative/).

#### Do I need Plex Pass to use Phlix?

No Plex Pass is needed on your home network. Away from home, Plex requires a Plex Pass (the server owner's or your own) or a Remote Watch Pass on your account to stream personal video remotely; Plex says music and photos stream remotely for free (Plex: Requirements for Remote Playback of Personal Media (https://support.plex.tv/articles/requirements-for-remote-playback-of-personal-media/)). Phlix itself needs only a Plex account and a Plex Media Server with at least one photo library, and it works with any Plex Media Server, with or without Plex Pass. Camera Upload needs no Plex Pass either. Phlix Pro is Phlix's own purchase in the App Store: Plex Pass does not include it.

#### How much does Phlix cost?

Phlix is free to download. Browsing, the timeline, search, favorites and on-device slideshows are free forever, with 25 saves to Photos and, from version 1.0.21, the first 100 camera uploads. Phlix Pro removes those limits and adds big-screen slideshows on your TV: $19.99 once, with Family Sharing, or $6.99 a year. You can try Pro free for 14 days; the trial never renews and never charges you.

#### Can I save photos from Plex into an album on my iPhone?

Yes. Pick an album once, and every photo you save from Phlix goes straight into it: Settings › Storage › Save to Album, or tap ••• on any photo and choose Save to Album. Pick one of your albums, or make a new one. Choosing an album asks iOS for full access to Photos, because albums need it. If you don't choose one, saves go to your library as before.

#### How many photos can Phlix handle?

Phlix is built for big libraries: it loads a page at a time instead of everything at once. Server-side year filtering, virtual paging and prefetching handle libraries of 100,000+ photos. The first screen appears in seconds; the year index fills in behind it.

#### How does the AirPlay slideshow work?

With Screen Mirroring on, or over an HDMI adapter, the TV shows just the photos while your iPhone shows the controls. Phlix draws its own full-screen window on the TV and asks your server for an image sized to the display, with hard cuts between photos. Choose 2, 4, 6 or 10 seconds a slide, shuffle and loop. This is a Phlix Pro feature; without Pro, the TV mirrors your iPhone's screen.

#### Which languages does Phlix speak?

English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese (Brazil), Dutch, Swedish, Danish, Norwegian, Finnish, Polish, Japanese, Korean, and Chinese, Simplified and Traditional. Phlix follows the language your iPhone or iPad is set to.

#### Does Phlix work on iPad and Mac?

Phlix is one app for iPhone and iPad; on iPad, a sidebar lists your libraries. On a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later, macOS 14 or later), the App Store offers the iPad version. Apple lists it as designed for iPad and not verified for macOS.

#### Is there a Phlix app for Apple TV or Android?

No. Phlix is an app for iPhone and iPad, and a Mac with Apple silicon can run the iPad version. To show your photos on a TV, turn on Screen Mirroring or use an HDMI adapter: with Phlix Pro, the TV shows just the photos while your iPhone shows the controls; without Pro, the TV mirrors your iPhone.

#### Does Phlix work with Jellyfin, Emby or Immich?

No. Phlix works with Plex Media Server only. It shows the photo libraries on your Plex server, and Camera Upload (Beta) backs up your iPhone or iPad into a folder of a Plex photo library.

#### Does Camera Upload work in the background?

Yes, as far as iOS allows. With Phlix closed, iOS gives it short bursts, mostly while the phone charges, so a large first backup takes a few days. With Phlix open on the Camera Upload screen and the phone on its charger, it uploads as fast as your Wi-Fi allows. It uploads only on your home Wi-Fi.

#### Is my data private with Phlix?

Yes. Phlix has no ads, no tracking pixels and no session replay. It sends anonymous usage, error and crash statistics tied to a random ID on your device, never your name, Plex account, photos, file names or server address, and you can turn that off in Settings. Camera Upload sends your photos only to the helper on your own server. See the Privacy Policy (https://phlixapp.com/privacy/) for full details.

#### What makes Phlix different from Plex Photos?

Plex Photos is Plex's own app; its App Store page lists a recommended view, a timeline view and a library view. Phlix is an independent app with folders that follow your server, a date timeline with a year scrubber, slideshows of a folder (with the folders inside it), a year or the whole library, saves to Photos or into an album, big-screen slideshows with Screen Mirroring or an HDMI adapter, a cellular data saver and, from version 1.0.21, Camera Upload (Beta).

#### Can I use Phlix outside my home network?

Yes, for browsing, as long as your Plex server allows remote access. Phlix connects to whichever server address is reachable, local or remote. For video, Plex requires a Plex Pass (the server owner's or your own) or a Remote Watch Pass to stream remotely; Plex says photos stream remotely for free (Plex: Requirements for Remote Playback of Personal Media (https://support.plex.tv/articles/requirements-for-remote-playback-of-personal-media/)). Some servers send only smaller copies of photos over the internet, so away from home a photo or a save can be a converted copy. Camera Upload is different on purpose: it uploads only on your home Wi-Fi.

#### Does the lifetime purchase include Family Sharing?

Yes. The $19.99 Pro Lifetime purchase is Family Shareable through Apple Family Sharing. Buy once and your whole family can use Pro on their devices.

#### What happens after the 14-day trial?

After 14 days, Phlix returns to the free tier: saves beyond your 25 free ones, camera uploads beyond your 100 free ones and big-screen slideshows need Pro again. You keep full access to browsing, the timeline, search, favorites and on-device slideshows. Nothing is deleted and nothing is charged. You can upgrade to Pro anytime.

#### Is Phlix made by Plex?

No. Phlix is an independent application and is not affiliated with, endorsed, or sponsored by Plex, Inc. It connects to your Plex Media Server using publicly available APIs.

## Plex Camera Upload: what happened, and what to use now (https://phlixapp.com/plex-camera-upload/)

Photos · Answers

Updated November 27, 2026 · 5 min read

### The short answer

Plex's own Camera Upload is gone. Plex announced on its forum in March 2021 that it was ending the feature, with removal targeted for June 2021.

To get the photos on your iPhone or iPad into Plex now, they have to land in a folder that one of your Plex photo libraries includes. Plex then scans them in like any other photo.

To do that automatically, use Camera Upload (Beta) in Phlix, an independent app that works with Plex Media Server. It copies your camera roll to a free helper that runs next to Plex Media Server, on your home Wi-Fi only, and the photos show up in your Plex photo library.

Camera Upload (Beta) needs Phlix 1.0.21 or later.

### What happened to Plex's Camera Upload?

Plex added Camera Upload to its mobile apps in 2014. It copied the photos on a phone to the owner's Plex Media Server. In March 2021, Plex posted Important info about Camera Upload in Plex in the Announcements section of its forum:

“Today we are ending support for the Camera Upload feature for those who do not have it enabled. Existing users that have it enabled may continue to use it as-is for now, but it will be removed in a future version of Plex. The current target for removal is 90 days from now (estimated June 2021).” The Plex Team, Plex Forum, Announcements, March 18, 2021 (archived copy (https://web.archive.org/web/20210319005631/https://forums.plex.tv/t/important-info-about-camera-upload-in-plex/700626); the original forum page is no longer online)

The same announcement said that photos already added through Camera Upload would not be affected, and gave Plex's reasons: many other apps now offered camera upload, and iOS and Android had brought “new formats, background processing APIs, and privacy restrictions on how apps like Plex are allowed to access users’ photos.”

The feature did not come back. In August 2025, when someone on Plex's forum asked whether the new Plex Photos app could upload the photos on their phone, a forum moderator answered: “That feature was discontinued about 4 years ago.” (Plex Forum, August 1, 2025 (https://forums.plex.tv/t/plex-photos-app-not-uploading-to-server/927683))

### How to get iPhone photos into Plex now

Plex shows the photos that are inside the folders of a Plex photo library, once it has scanned them. So every way of getting phone photos into Plex comes down to one thing: putting the files into such a folder. There are two ways to do that.

#### 1. Automatically, at home: Camera Upload (Beta) in Phlix

Camera Upload in Phlix backs up the photos and videos on your iPhone or iPad to the server in your home, while the device is on your home Wi-Fi. It has two parts. The Phlix app on the phone reads your camera roll. A small free program on your server, the Camera Upload helper, receives the photos and writes them into a folder of your Plex photo library. The helper is one Docker container, and its source code is public.
- Only at home. Phlix uploads on your home Wi-Fi and nowhere else. Never over mobile data.
- Only to you. Photos go from your phone straight to your server, encrypted. None of them go to Phlix or to a cloud service.
- Only copies. Nothing is ever deleted or changed on your phone.
- In your Plex library. Each device gets its own folder, with a folder for each year and month, so the photos show up in Plex, and in Phlix, next to everything else.

The helper is free. In the app, the first 100 uploads are free, and Phlix Pro (https://phlixapp.com/#pricing) uploads the rest. Camera Upload is a beta: keep your own backup of anything you cannot replace. What the beta does, and what it does not do (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#beta).

#### 2. By hand, now and then

Without an app, copy the photos yourself, then let Plex scan:
- From the iPhone. In the Files app, connect to a shared folder on your server (Browse, then the ••• button, then Connect to Server). Then in the Photos app, select the photos, tap Share, and choose Save to Files with that folder.
- From a computer. Import the photos from the iPhone to the computer, then copy them into the folder of your Plex photo library.
- Then, in Plex, scan the photo library, or switch on Settings › Library › Scan my library automatically so that Plex picks up new files by itself. That setting depends on the server noticing new files, which typically fails for folders mounted over the network; then also switch on Scan my library periodically (Plex: Library settings (https://support.plex.tv/articles/200289526-library/)).

That works, and it needs nothing new on your server. It is also easy to forget, which is what Camera Upload is for.

### Camera Upload (Beta) in three steps

#### Install the helper

One Docker container on the machine that runs Plex Media Server, pointed at a folder inside your Plex photo library.

#### Connect your iPhone

In Phlix, open Settings › Camera Upload. Phlix finds the helper on your network and pairs with it.

#### At home

On your home Wi-Fi, new photos copy to your server: straight away while Phlix is open, and in short bursts while it is closed.

On a Linux computer or server, or a Mac with Docker Desktop, step 1 is one command in a terminal on the server. The installer checks Docker, asks for your upload folder and starts the helper:

```
curl -fsSL https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/install.sh | sh
```

On Windows, Unraid, Synology, TrueNAS SCALE and QNAP, or to let an AI assistant do it, follow the setup guide's Step 1 (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#install). Then, in Phlix, tap Check for the Helper, then Check My Network. Nothing is switched on, and nothing is uploaded, until the helper is found. When Phlix says Helper found, name this device's folder and tap Connect. The owner of the Plex server pairs without a code; family members type the helper's pairing code. All the steps, with screenshots (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#connect).

### Where the photos go

Each phone or tablet gets its own folder inside the upload folder, with one folder for each year and one for each month:

```
Camera Uploads/
  Anna's iPhone/
    2026/
      2026-11/
        IMG_1234.HEIC
        IMG_1235.MOV
```

A file keeps its name and its date. The same photo from two phones is stored once, and nothing is ever overwritten. When your Plex account owns the server, Phlix asks Plex to scan once your photos have arrived. To be sure, switch on Scan my library automatically in Plex as well.

### Questions

#### Does Plex still have Camera Upload?

No. Plex announced on its forum on March 18, 2021 that it was ending support for Camera Upload, with removal targeted for June 2021. In August 2025, a moderator on Plex's forum described the feature as discontinued about four years earlier. Photos uploaded before that stayed in Plex.

#### How do I back up my iPhone photos to Plex automatically?

Camera Upload (Beta) in Phlix does it. Install the free Phlix Camera Upload helper, one Docker container, on the machine that runs Plex Media Server, and point it at a folder inside your Plex photo library. Then turn on Settings > Camera Upload in Phlix. At home, on your Wi-Fi, new photos copy to your server by themselves. It needs Phlix 1.0.21 or later.

#### Can I put iPhone photos into Plex without an app?

Yes, by hand. Copy the photos into a folder that one of your Plex photo libraries includes, then let Plex scan the library. From an iPhone, the Files app can connect to a shared folder on your server, and in the Photos app, Share > Save to Files copies the selected photos there. From a computer, import the photos from the iPhone and copy them into that folder.

#### Does Phlix Camera Upload need Plex Pass?

No. The helper writes ordinary files into a folder of your Plex photo library, which works with every Plex Media Server.

#### Does it upload away from home or over mobile data?

No, on purpose. Phlix uploads only while the iPhone or iPad is on your home Wi-Fi. Away from home it does not start uploads or look for your server, apart from rare cases that the privacy policy (https://phlixapp.com/privacy/#camera-upload) lists; even then, your photos go only to your own helper. Photos you take on a trip upload when you are back.

#### Does it delete photos from my iPhone?

No. It is a one-way copy. Phlix never deletes or changes anything in your Photo Library, and deleting a photo on the phone leaves the copy on the server.

#### What does it cost?

The helper is free, and its source code is public. In the app, the first 100 uploads are free, and Phlix Pro uploads the rest: $19.99 once, with Family Sharing, or $6.99 a year, with a 14-day free trial that never charges you.

#### What do I need?

Plex Media Server with a photo library, on a computer or NAS that runs Docker (Linux, a Mac or Windows PC with Docker Desktop, Synology, Unraid, TrueNAS SCALE or QNAP); Phlix 1.0.21 or later on an iPhone or iPad; and the phone and the server on the same home network.

#### Is Phlix made by Plex?

No. Phlix is an independent application and is not affiliated with, endorsed, or sponsored by Plex, Inc. It works with Plex Media Server.

#### Is there an Android version?

No. Phlix is an app for iPhone and iPad.

## A Plex Photos alternative for iPhone and iPad (https://phlixapp.com/plex-photos-alternative/)

Photos · Answers

Updated November 27, 2026 · 4 min read

### The short answer

Phlix is an independent iPhone and iPad app that works with Plex Media Server. It shows the photos and videos in your Plex photo libraries by folder or on a date timeline with a year scrubber, saves them to the Photos app or straight into an album, and plays slideshows of a folder (with the folders inside it), a year or the whole library.

With Screen Mirroring on, or over an HDMI adapter, the TV shows just the photos while your iPhone shows the controls (Phlix Pro; without Pro, the TV mirrors the phone). From version 1.0.21, Camera Upload (Beta) also backs up your camera roll to your Plex server at home.

Phlix is free to browse, so you can try it on your own library. Camera Upload needs Phlix 1.0.21 or later.

### Plex Photos and Phlix

Plex Photos is Plex's own free app for photo libraries. Its App Store page lists three supported features: Recommended View, Timeline View and Library View. Its latest version is 2025.2.0, from June 12, 2025.

Phlix reads the same photo libraries on the same Plex Media Server. You do not have to choose: Phlix never changes or deletes what is on your server, so you can use it next to any Plex app. Here is what each one lists:

| Feature | Phlix | Plex Photos |
| Timeline by date | Yes, with a year scrubber | Timeline View |
| Folders as on your server | Yes | Library View |
| Save to the Photos app, or into an album | 25 free, unlimited with Pro | Not listed |
| Slideshows of a folder, a year or the whole library | 2, 4, 6 or 10 seconds a slide, shuffle, loop | Not listed |
| Just the photos on the TV, the controls on the iPhone | With Screen Mirroring or an HDMI adapter (Pro) | Not listed |
| Camera upload to your own server | Beta, from version 1.0.21 | Not listed |
| Curated highlights | No | Recommended View |

The Plex Photos column is what Plex lists on its App Store page (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/plex-photos/id6504519803), checked November 24, 2026. "Not listed" means the page does not list it.

### What Phlix does
- Folders and a timeline. Folders that follow the folders on your server, and a date timeline one tap away. Tap a year on the scrubber, say 1987, to see just that year.
- Built for big libraries. Phlix loads a page at a time instead of everything at once, so a library of 100,000 photos opens in seconds.
- Save to Photos and Save to Album. Save photos and videos to the Photos app, one at a time: the original file when your server sends it, or a copy your server converted, which may be smaller. Pick an album once, and every save goes into it.
- Slideshows. A folder's slideshow also plays the folders inside it (switch: Include Subfolders). 2, 4, 6 or 10 seconds a slide, shuffle and loop, with hard cuts between photos.
- Big-screen slideshows. With Screen Mirroring on, or over an HDMI adapter, the TV shows just the photos while your iPhone shows the controls. A Phlix Pro feature; without Pro, the TV mirrors your phone.
- Camera Upload (Beta). From version 1.0.21, Phlix backs up the photos and videos on your iPhone or iPad to a folder of your Plex photo library, on your home Wi-Fi only, through a free helper next to Plex Media Server. What happened to Plex's own Camera Upload, and how this one works (https://phlixapp.com/plex-camera-upload/).
- Search and favorites. Search photo and video titles, tags and collections. Favorites are saved on your device.
- Your server, or a shared one. Use your own server or one shared with you, and switch between its photo libraries.
- Every screen. iPhone and iPad, with a sidebar of your libraries on iPad, VoiceOver support, and English and 15 more languages.
- Careful with data. On cellular and in Low Data Mode, Phlix stops loading ahead of you.

### What Phlix does not do
- It plays photo libraries only: not your movie, TV or music libraries.
- It does not edit photos, and it never changes or deletes what is on your server. Camera Upload only adds new files, in the folder you choose for it.
- It does not convert files itself. HEIC, RAW and TIFF photos are converted by your Plex server; if it cannot convert one, Phlix shows the best copy it can get.
- It is not on Android.

### What it costs

Phlix is free to download and free to browse, with no ads. Browsing, the timeline, search, favorites and on-device slideshows are free forever, with 25 saves to Photos and, from version 1.0.21, the first 100 camera uploads. Phlix Pro (https://phlixapp.com/#pricing) removes those limits and adds big-screen slideshows on your TV: $19.99 once, with Family Sharing, or $6.99 a year. Try Pro free for 14 days: the trial is not a subscription, and it never charges you.

### How to try it on your own library
- Download Phlix from the App Store.
- Sign in on Plex's own sign-in page. Phlix never sees your password, and there is no Phlix account to create.
- Pick your server and a photo library. Phlix needs a Plex Media Server with at least one photo library, and iOS 17 or later.

### Questions

#### Is there an alternative to the Plex Photos app?

Yes. Phlix is an independent iPhone and iPad app that works with Plex Media Server. It shows the photos and videos in your Plex photo libraries by folder or on a date timeline with a year scrubber, saves them to the Photos app or into an album, and plays slideshows on the phone or on your TV. It is free to browse.

#### Is Phlix made by Plex?

No. Phlix is an independent application and is not affiliated with, endorsed, or sponsored by Plex, Inc. It works with Plex Media Server.

#### Can I use Phlix and Plex Photos side by side?

Yes. Both read the same photo libraries on your Plex Media Server. Phlix never changes or deletes what is on your server, so you can keep using any Plex app next to it.

#### Do I need Plex Pass?

No Plex Pass is needed on your home network. For video, Plex requires a Plex Pass (the server owner's or your own) or a Remote Watch Pass to stream remotely; Plex says photos stream remotely for free (Plex: Requirements for Remote Playback of Personal Media (https://support.plex.tv/articles/requirements-for-remote-playback-of-personal-media/)). Some servers send only smaller copies of photos over the internet, so away from home a photo or a save can be a converted copy.

#### Does Phlix work with a Plex server that someone shared with me?

Yes. Use your own server or one shared with you, and switch between its photo libraries.

#### How much does Phlix cost?

Phlix is free to browse, with 25 free saves to Photos. Phlix Pro adds unlimited saves, big-screen slideshows on your TV and, from version 1.0.21, unlimited camera uploads: $19.99 once, with Family Sharing, or $6.99 a year. You can try Pro free for 14 days; the trial never renews and never charges you.

#### Can Phlix upload the photos on my iPhone to Plex?

Yes, from version 1.0.21: Camera Upload (Beta) copies the photos and videos on your iPhone or iPad into a folder of your Plex photo library, on your home Wi-Fi only, through a free helper you run in Docker next to Plex Media Server.

#### Does Phlix work on iPad and Mac?

Phlix is one app for iPhone and iPad; on iPad, a sidebar lists your libraries. On a Mac with Apple silicon, the App Store offers the iPad version. Apple lists it as designed for iPad and not verified for macOS.

#### Which languages does Phlix speak?

English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese (Brazil), Dutch, Swedish, Danish, Norwegian, Finnish, Polish, Japanese, Korean, and Chinese, Simplified and Traditional.

#### Phlix: a photo app that works with Plex Media Server

Folders and a date timeline, saves to Photos or an album, and slideshows on your TV. Free to browse, with no ads. Download Phlix Free (https://apps.apple.com/app/phlix-photos/id6796820208)

## Support: frequently asked questions (https://phlixapp.com/support/)

#### What do I need to use Phlix?

A Plex account (free or Plex Pass; see remote access below) and a Plex Media Server with at least one photo library. Your device must be running iOS 17 or later.

#### How much does Phlix cost?

Phlix is free to download. Browsing your library, the timeline, search, favorites and on-device slideshows are free forever, with 25 saves to the Photos app and the first 100 camera uploads (Camera Upload is a beta, in Phlix 1.0.21 or later). Phlix Pro removes those limits and adds big-screen slideshows on your TV: a one-time $19.99 purchase, with Family Sharing, or $6.99/year. You can also try Pro free for 14 days with no subscription and no charge.

#### How do I install Phlix on another device?

Phlix is free to download on any device. If you purchased Phlix Pro (lifetime), it is tied to your Apple ID and available on any device signed into the same account, including through Apple Family Sharing.

#### I don't see any photo libraries.

Phlix only displays photo-type libraries from your Plex server. Make sure your Plex Media Server has at least one library with the type set to "Photos." You can add one in your Plex server's settings.

#### Can I use Phlix outside my home network?

Yes, as long as your Plex server allows remote access. Phlix connects to whichever server address is reachable — local or remote. For video, Plex requires a Plex Pass (the server owner's or your own) or a Remote Watch Pass to stream remotely; Plex says photos stream remotely for free (Plex: Requirements for Remote Playback of Personal Media (https://support.plex.tv/articles/requirements-for-remote-playback-of-personal-media/)). Some servers send only smaller copies of photos over the internet, so away from home a photo or a save can be a converted copy.

#### Does Phlix work with Plex Pass?

Yes. Phlix works with any Plex Media Server, with or without Plex Pass, and needs no Plex Pass on your home network or for Camera Upload. Away from home, Plex requires a Plex Pass (the server owner's or your own) or a Remote Watch Pass on your account to stream personal video remotely; Plex says music and photos stream remotely for free (Plex: Requirements for Remote Playback of Personal Media (https://support.plex.tv/articles/requirements-for-remote-playback-of-personal-media/)). Phlix Pro is Phlix's own purchase in the App Store: Plex Pass does not include it.

#### Is Phlix made by Plex?

No. Phlix is an independent application and is not affiliated with, endorsed, or sponsored by Plex, Inc. Plex, the Plex Play logo, and Plex Media Server are trademarks of Plex GmbH and used under a license. Phlix uses Plex's publicly available API to connect to your server.

#### How do I clear the image cache?

Go to Settings > Storage > Clear Image Cache. This frees up disk space without affecting your favorites or preferences.

#### What does Camera Upload (Beta) do?

It backs up the photos and videos on your iPhone or iPad to a folder of your Plex photo library, on your own server. It uploads only on your home Wi-Fi, never over mobile data. The connection is encrypted, and your photos go to your own server and nowhere else. It is a one-way copy: it never deletes or changes anything on your device. On the server each device has its own folder, with a folder for each year and month. The first 100 uploads are free, and Phlix Pro uploads the rest. It does not upload the video part of a Live Photo, hidden photos, shared albums, or photos synced from a computer. It is a beta: keep your own backup of anything you cannot replace. The setup guide (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#beta) lists what the beta does and what it does not do.

#### How do I set up Camera Upload (Beta)?

Camera Upload backs up the photos and videos on your iPhone or iPad to your own server, on your home Wi-Fi only. It needs Phlix 1.0.21 or later, and a small free program, the helper, that you run in Docker on your own server, next to Plex Media Server. The Camera Upload setup guide (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/) has every step, with networking help and troubleshooting. It is also in German (https://phlixapp.com/de/camera-upload/), French (https://phlixapp.com/fr/camera-upload/), Spanish (https://phlixapp.com/es/camera-upload/), Japanese (https://phlixapp.com/ja/camera-upload/) and the other languages of the app: see the language list at the top of the guide.

#### Is this Plex's own Camera Upload?

No. Plex announced in March 2021 that it was ending its own Camera Upload. Camera Upload in Phlix is a separate feature of an independent app that works with Plex Media Server: it copies your photos into a folder of your Plex photo library through the helper on your own server. What happened to Plex's Camera Upload (https://phlixapp.com/plex-camera-upload/).

#### Can I try new versions before they are released?

Yes. Before a new version reaches the App Store, a small group of testers can try it through TestFlight, Apple's app for beta versions. Ask to become a beta tester (https://phlixapp.com/beta/).

## Save to Photos (https://phlixapp.com/features/save-to-photos/)

Feature · Save to Photos

Updated November 27, 2026

Phlix downloads the photos and videos on your Plex Media Server into the Photos app on your iPhone or iPad, or straight into an album you choose. Once saved, they stay on your device whether or not your server is reachable.
- Photos and videos. Open one and tap ••• to save it, or long-press it in a folder or on the timeline.
- Into an album, if you like. Choose an album once, and every save goes into it.
- 25 saves free. Phlix Pro saves without a limit.

Download Phlix Free (https://apps.apple.com/app/phlix-photos/id6796820208)

### Save a photo or a video

Open a photo or video in Phlix and tap •••. The menu has three ways to keep it:
- Save to Photos saves it now. Phlix then says it is saved, and how many free saves you have left.
- Download saves it to Photos in the background, so you can keep browsing.
- Save to Album… chooses the album your saves go into.

### Straight into an album

Choose an album once, under Settings › Storage › Save to Album, or with Save to Album… on any photo. Every photo you save from Phlix then goes into it. Pick one of your albums or make a new one, and choose No Album to stop.

Albums need full access to your photo library, so choosing one asks iOS for it.

### The original file, when your server sends it

Phlix asks your Plex server for the original file, and when the server sends it, that is what you get. When it cannot, Phlix saves the copy your server converts, which may be smaller. A file in a format the Photos app cannot store can go to the Files app instead.

### Why save a photo to your iPhone
- To share it. Messages, mail and other apps share from your photo library, and cannot reach your Plex server.
- To have it with you. A saved photo stays on your iPhone when your server is off or out of reach.
- To edit it. The Photos app's editing tools work on saved photos.

### How to save a photo from your Plex server to your iPhone
- Download Phlix free from the App Store and sign in with your Plex account, on Plex's own sign-in page.
- Open a photo or video from your server, in a folder or on the timeline.
- Tap ••• and choose Save to Photos.
- Find it in the Photos app with your other photos, or in the album you chose.

### Free and Pro

#### Free
- 25 saves to Photos, photos and videos alike
- Browsing, the timeline, search, favorites and slideshows on your device

#### Phlix Pro
- Unlimited saves to Photos
- Unlimited uploads with Camera Upload (Beta)
- Slideshows that fill your TV

Phlix Pro is $19.99 once, with Family Sharing, or $6.99 a year. Try it free for 14 days: the trial is not a subscription and never charges you. Prices are in US dollars and differ by country.

### Questions

#### Can I download photos from my Plex server to my iPhone?

Yes. Phlix, an iPhone and iPad app that works with Plex Media Server, saves the photos and videos on your server into the Photos app, or into an album you choose. The first 25 saves are free, and Phlix Pro saves without a limit.

#### Can I save videos too?

Yes. Videos save to the Photos app the same way as photos.

#### Does Phlix save the original file?

When your Plex server sends the original, yes. When it cannot, Phlix saves the copy your server converts, which may be smaller. A file in a format the Photos app cannot store can be saved to the Files app instead.

#### Where do saved photos go?

Into the Photos app on your iPhone or iPad, with your other photos, or into the album you chose under Settings, Storage, Save to Album. They stay there if you delete Phlix.

#### Will Camera Upload send saved photos back to my server?

No. Since version 1.0.21, Phlix keeps a list of the photos it saves from your server, and Camera Upload on that device does not upload them back.

## Timeline (https://phlixapp.com/features/timeline/)

Feature · Timeline

Updated November 27, 2026

Phlix shows the photos and videos in your Plex photo library on one timeline, sorted by date, with the years down the side: tap 1987 and you are there. It is built for libraries of 100,000 photos and more.
- A year scrubber. Tap a year to jump straight to it.
- Built for big libraries. Phlix loads a page at a time instead of everything at once.
- Free. Browsing and the timeline are free, with no ads.

Download Phlix Free (https://apps.apple.com/app/phlix-photos/id6796820208)

### Jump to any year

The years run down the side of the timeline. Tap one and the timeline jumps there, so decades of photos are a tap apart. It works the way the Photos app does, with the photos on your own server.

### Built for 100,000 photos and more

Phlix loads a page at a time instead of your whole library at once. The first screen appears in seconds, and the year index fills in behind it, even in a very large library.

On cellular data and in Low Data Mode, Phlix stops loading ahead of you. On Wi-Fi it loads at full quality.

### Folders or the timeline

Phlix also shows your library the way your server has it: the same folders, in the same order. One tap switches between the folders and the timeline.

### Open, zoom, play

Tap a photo to see it full screen, pinch to zoom, and swipe to the next one. Videos play in a player that remembers where you stopped.

### Questions

#### Can I see my Plex photos by date on an iPhone?

Yes. Phlix shows the photos in your Plex photo library on a date timeline with a year scrubber, on iPhone and iPad. Browsing is free.

#### Does it work with a very large library?

Yes. Phlix is built for libraries of 100,000 photos and more. It loads a page at a time, so the first screen appears in seconds.

#### Can I still browse by folder?

Yes. One tap switches between the timeline and the folders on your server, in the same order as on the server.

#### Does Phlix change my library?

No. Phlix never changes or deletes what is on your server.

Updated November 27, 2026

- Your pace. 2, 4, 6 or 10 seconds a slide, with shuffle and loop.

## Browse and Search (https://phlixapp.com/features/browse-and-search/)

Feature · Browse and Search

Updated November 27, 2026

Phlix shows the folders on your Plex server exactly as you organized them, and searches photo and video titles, tags and collections across your library. Mark the keepers with a heart: favorites are saved on your device.
- The same folders as your server. In the same order, with a path at the top.
- Search. Titles, tags and collections, across the library.
- Your server or a shared one. Switch between its photo libraries.

Download Phlix Free (https://apps.apple.com/app/phlix-photos/id6796820208)

### The folders you organized

Phlix follows the folders on your server, in the same order, with the path at the top so you always know where you are. A folder's slideshow is one tap away.

### Search the whole library

Search photo and video titles, tags and collections, and open any result full screen.

### Favorites

Tap the heart on a photo or video to keep it close. Favorites are saved on your device and have their own tab.

### Full screen, photos and clips

Swipe through a day or a folder, pinch to zoom, and play video clips in a player that remembers where you stopped. HEIC, RAW and TIFF photos are converted by your Plex server; if it cannot convert one, Phlix falls back to another copy the server can send.

### Your server, or one shared with you

Use your own Plex Media Server or one shared with you, and switch between its photo libraries. On iPad, a sidebar lists your libraries. A Mac with Apple silicon can run the iPad version from the App Store.

Phlix shows photo libraries only: it does not play your movie, TV or music libraries.

### Questions

#### Does Phlix work with a Plex server shared with me?

Yes. Use your own Plex Media Server or one shared with you, and switch between its photo libraries.

#### Does Phlix play movies or music from Plex?

No. Phlix shows photo libraries only.

#### Can I use Phlix on an iPad or a Mac?

Yes. On iPad, a sidebar lists your libraries. A Mac with Apple silicon can run the iPad version from the App Store.

#### Does Phlix change anything on my server?

No. Phlix never changes or deletes what is on your server. Camera Upload (Beta) only adds new files, in the folder you choose for it.

## Camera Upload (Beta) setup guide (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/)

Beta · Setup guide

Updated November 27, 2026 · About 10 minutes to set up

On your iPhone or iPad? Step 1 is done on your server: open phlixapp.com/camera-upload on a computer to copy the commands. Helper installed already? Go to Step 2: Connect your iPhone (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#connect). Something not working? See Troubleshooting (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#troubleshooting).

Camera Upload backs up the photos and videos on your iPhone or iPad to the server in your home, while the device is on your home Wi-Fi. They show up in Plex, and in Phlix, next to everything else. No cloud and no storage subscription.

Camera Upload is a beta in Phlix 1.0.21 or later: keep your own backup of anything you cannot replace. See what the beta does and what it does not do. (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#beta)

Camera Upload has two parts. The Phlix app on your iPhone or iPad reads your camera roll. A small free program on your server, the Camera Upload helper, receives the photos and writes them into a folder of your Plex photo library. The helper is one Docker container, and this page shows three ways to install it.

Plex had a Camera Upload of its own, and announced in March 2021 that it was ending it. Camera Upload in Phlix is a separate feature of an independent app that works with Plex Media Server. What happened to Plex's Camera Upload, and the other ways to get iPhone photos into Plex (https://phlixapp.com/plex-camera-upload/).
- Only at home. Phlix uploads on your home Wi-Fi and nowhere else. Never over mobile data.
- Only to you. Photos go from your phone straight to your server, encrypted. None of them go to Phlix.
- Only copies. Nothing is ever deleted or changed on your phone.
- Free to try. The helper is free, and so are the first 100 uploads. Phlix Pro (https://phlixapp.com/#pricing) uploads the rest.

### How it works

#### Install the helper (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#install)

One Docker container on the machine that runs Plex Media Server. You point it at a folder inside your Plex photo library.

#### Connect your iPhone (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#connect)

In Phlix, open Settings › Camera Upload. Phlix finds the helper on your network and pairs with it once: from then on, the helper takes photos only from paired devices, and Phlix talks only to that helper.

#### Back up at home (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#after)

On your home Wi-Fi, new photos copy to your server: straight away while Phlix is open, and in short bursts while it is closed. Phlix shows what is backed up and tells you when everything is.

### What Camera Upload does, and does not do

Camera Upload is a beta in Phlix 1.0.21 or later: it works, and it is new. Keep your own backup of anything you cannot replace, and tell us what goes wrong on the support page (https://phlixapp.com/support/).

#### What it does
- Backs up the photos and videos in the Photo Library of your iPhone or iPad to a folder of your Plex photo library, on your own server. You choose what to back up: Include Videos (on at first), Include Screenshots (off at first), and Everything on this device or Only new photos.
- Copies each photo as it looks in Photos at that moment: an edited photo uploads edited, a Live Photo as its still photo. It never deletes or changes anything on the device.
- Checks before it starts. Phlix looks for the helper at your Plex server's address on port 7459, or at an address you type. If the helper is not found, Camera Upload stays off and Phlix says why.
- Pairs with proof. The owner of the Plex server pairs without a code; everyone else types the helper's pairing code (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#pairing). The connection is encrypted (HTTPS), and Phlix talks only to the helper whose certificate it saw when it paired: a certificate is the helper's proof of who it is.
- Uploads only on your home Wi-Fi: the network the device was on when it paired, or one you add with This Is My Home Network. With Phlix open, new photos are picked up and uploaded by themselves.
- Shows where you stand: a green dot and "Connected to" the helper's name when the connection is good; how many items are backed up out of how many, how many are still to back up, what is uploading now, what was backed up recently, and how many could not be backed up. It says Everything is backed up when it is, and sends a notification too if you switch on Notify Me When Backed Up.
- Keeps a folder for each device, with a folder for each year and month. A file keeps its name and its date. The same photo from two devices is stored once. Nothing is ever overwritten. When your Plex account owns the server, Phlix asks Plex to scan once your photos have arrived, so they show up in Plex.
- Needs one free helper: one Docker container, for Intel, AMD and Arm processors, with a read-only status page and a doctor command that checks the install and says how to fix what is wrong. It has no account and no cloud service.
- The first 100 uploads are free. Phlix Pro (https://phlixapp.com/#pricing) uploads the rest.

#### What it does not do
- It does not upload away from home, over mobile data, or through a VPN into your home.
- It is not a sync. Deleting a photo on the phone leaves the copy on the server, and nothing comes back to the phone.
- It does not upload the video part of a Live Photo, hidden photos, shared albums, or photos synced from a computer.
- It does not find the helper by itself when the helper is on another machine or another port than Plex. You type the address once.
- With Phlix closed, it uploads only when iOS allows it: in short bursts, mostly while the device charges. A large library takes a few days in the background.
- It works on iPhone and iPad only, and on home networks that use IPv4 addresses, such as 192.168.1.10. A network with only IPv6 is not supported.

### What you need
- Plex Media Server with a photo library, on a computer or NAS that runs Docker. Docker is a program that runs other programs in closed boxes called containers. It is free for personal use, and the helper comes as one container. The helper needs Docker 20.10 or later. Intel, AMD and Arm processors all work. It runs on Linux, on a Mac or Windows PC with Docker Desktop, and on Unraid, Synology (some models), TrueNAS SCALE and QNAP.

#### Docker on your system: what to install first, and what to check

  - Linux: install Docker with Docker's own instructions (https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/), not from a Snap: Docker from a Snap, which Ubuntu Server offers while it installs, cannot start the helper. If snap list docker lists docker, The helper does not start (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#ts-start) says how to replace it. You also need Docker Compose version 2, the docker compose command: the part of Docker that starts a program from one small text file. If docker compose version does not answer, add it (https://docs.docker.com/compose/install/). If you installed Ubuntu's own package with sudo apt install docker.io, add Ubuntu's Compose package instead: sudo apt install docker-compose-v2 (in Ubuntu 22.04 and later).
  - Mac or Windows PC: install Docker Desktop (https://docs.docker.com/desktop/) and start it. Docker Compose comes with it. The helper runs only while Docker Desktop runs.
  - Synology: install Container Manager from Package Center. It needs DSM 7.2 or later, and Synology offers it only on some models: see the Synology steps (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#sys-synology).
  - Unraid: Docker is part of Unraid. You do not need Docker Compose there.
  - TrueNAS SCALE 24.10 or later: Docker is part of it.
  - QNAP: install Container Station from App Center. The steps on this page are for Container Station 3, which needs QTS 5.1 or QuTS hero h5.1 or later.

- Phlix 1.0.21 or later on an iPhone or iPad.
- Your phone and your server on the same home network.

The helper is free. In the app, the first 100 uploads are free, and Phlix Pro (https://phlixapp.com/#pricing) uploads the rest.

### Step 1: Install the helper

Reading this on your phone? Step 1 is done on your server. Open phlixapp.com/camera-upload on a computer, so that you can copy the commands.

Do this once, on the machine that runs Plex Media Server. First, decide on your upload folder: the folder where your phone's photos will go. It must be inside a folder that one of your Plex photo libraries includes, or Plex never shows the photos. To see your library's folders, open Plex in a browser, go to Settings › Manage › Libraries, choose Edit Library on your photo library, then Add folders. If the folder there is /mnt/media/Photos, a good choice is /mnt/media/Photos/Camera Uploads.

Does your Plex run in Docker itself? That is usual on Unraid and TrueNAS SCALE. Plex then shows the folder's path inside its own container, such as /data/Photos. The helper needs the folder's path on the server, such as /mnt/media/Photos. Read Plex itself runs in Docker (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#sys-plex-docker) before you go on.

Then find your system. It decides which steps you follow.
- A Linux computer or server: way A, B or C below.
- A Mac with Docker Desktop: way A, B or C below. Read the note for Mac and Windows (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#sys-desktop) first.
- A Windows PC with Docker Desktop: way B or C below. Read the note for Mac and Windows (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#sys-desktop) first. Way A is for Linux and macOS.
- Unraid: the Unraid steps (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#sys-unraid), or way B. Unraid has no Docker Compose, so ways A and C do not work there.
- Synology: the Synology steps (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#sys-synology), which use Container Manager in place of the command line, or way B.
- TrueNAS SCALE: the TrueNAS SCALE steps (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#sys-truenas), or way B. Do not use way A there: let TrueNAS manage the helper.
- QNAP: the QNAP steps (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#sys-qnap), which use Container Station in place of the command line. Way B's instructions do not cover QNAP.

#### New to typing commands? Where to type them

The commands on this page are typed into a terminal: a window where you type a line and press Return. Type them on your server, the machine that runs Plex Media Server.
- Linux with a screen: open the terminal program. It is often named Terminal.
- Linux without a screen: sign in from another computer with SSH, a way to type commands on one computer from another. In a terminal on the other computer, type ssh NAME@SERVER, with your user name on the server and the server's address.
- Mac: open the app named Terminal. It is in Applications › Utilities.
- Windows: open PowerShell.
- Unraid, Synology, TrueNAS SCALE and QNAP: read Steps and notes for your system (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#platforms), below, first. It says where to type commands on each, and the install steps differ there.

A command in a box has a Copy button. Paste the command into the terminal and press Return.

If Docker answers "permission denied", put sudo in front of each docker command. sudo runs one command as the administrator and may ask for your password. If the one-command installer needs this, it stops and shows the command to use.

#### A. Run one command (Quickest)

For a Linux computer or server, and for a Mac with Docker Desktop. Not for Windows, Unraid, TrueNAS SCALE or QNAP: find your system in the list above.

Paste this into a terminal on your server:

```
curl -fsSL https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/install.sh | sh
```

The installer checks Docker and asks for your upload folder. It writes the Compose file, docker-compose.yml, into a new folder named phlix-camera-upload in your home folder. The Compose file is a small text file that tells Docker how to run the helper. Then the installer starts the helper and runs its check. When all is well, it prints Phlix Camera Upload is running. and, under that, a line that starts with Status page: with the address of the helper's status page.

It never uses sudo, never changes Plex and never deletes a photo. You can read the script (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/install.sh) before you run it (if your browser saves it instead of showing it, read it on GitHub (https://github.com/jrl8085/phlix-camera-upload/blob/main/install.sh)), and try it first with --dry-run, which changes nothing:

```
curl -fsSL https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/install.sh | sh -s -- --dry-run
```

#### Install without questions, or update later

To answer the installer's questions ahead of time, for example where there is no terminal to ask on, give it your upload folder with --photos and add --yes. It then asks nothing, and it makes the folder if it is missing. Put your own upload folder in place of the example:

```
curl -fsSL https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/install.sh | sh -s -- --photos "/mnt/media/Photos/Camera Uploads" --yes
```

Run the installer again at any time to update the helper. If you installed with --photos and --yes, leave both out when you update: the installer then keeps your Compose file as it is. With them, it can write a new Compose file that keeps only your upload folder, port, PLEX_URL, PUID and PGID. The old file stays next to the new one.

Done when the installer prints Phlix Camera Upload is running. Next: check that the helper runs (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#check).

#### B. Let an AI assistant do it

For anyone who would rather answer questions than edit files.

The file SETUP-WITH-AI.md (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/SETUP-WITH-AI.md) holds complete instructions written for an AI assistant: how to find your Plex library's folder, install the helper, check it, and fix what goes wrong. The assistant asks before it changes anything outside the helper's own folder, and it is told never to touch Plex itself or to open anything to the internet.

##### Any assistant that can run commands on your server

Such as Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or Cursor. Download the instructions into a new, empty folder on your server:

```
curl -fsSLO https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/SETUP-WITH-AI.md
```

Then start your assistant in that folder and say: Follow SETUP-WITH-AI.md

##### Claude Code, as a skill

Add the skill once, from a terminal:

```
claude plugin marketplace add jrl8085/phlix-camera-upload
claude plugin install phlix-camera-upload@phlix
```

Then start Claude Code on your server and say: Set up Phlix Camera Upload on this server. The same skill helps later, too: ask it to check, update or fix the helper.

##### A chat assistant, such as ChatGPT or the Claude app

Give it the file SETUP-WITH-AI.md (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/SETUP-WITH-AI.md) and say: Walk me through this, one step at a time. It tells you each command, you run it on your server and paste back what it printed. In the Claude apps you can also add the setup skill itself: download phlix-camera-upload-setup.zip (https://github.com/jrl8085/phlix-camera-upload/releases/latest/download/phlix-camera-upload-setup.zip) and upload it under Customize › Skills.

Done when the assistant says Phlix Camera Upload is running. and gives you the status page's address. Next: check that the helper runs (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#check).

#### C. Do it by hand, with Docker Compose

For people who like to see every step, on Linux, a Mac or a Windows PC. Six steps, one line to edit. Unraid, Synology, TrueNAS SCALE and QNAP have their own steps below.
- Make your upload folder, as the user who owns your photos: the helper writes files as the owner of this folder. Put your own path in place of the example:

```
mkdir "/mnt/media/Photos/Camera Uploads"
```
 On Linux, if mkdir says "Permission denied", your user may not write to your library's folder, for example because it belongs to root, or to plex, the user that runs Plex Media Server. Make the folder with sudo, and give it the owner of the folder above it. Put your own paths in place of the examples:

```
sudo mkdir "/mnt/media/Photos/Camera Uploads"
sudo chown --reference="/mnt/media/Photos" "/mnt/media/Photos/Camera Uploads"
```

- Make a folder for the helper and go into it.

```
mkdir phlix-camera-upload
cd phlix-camera-upload
```

- Download the Compose file, docker-compose.yml: a small text file that tells Docker how to run the helper.

```
curl -fsSLO https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/docker-compose.yml
```

- Open docker-compose.yml in a text editor. Find the line source: /CHANGE/THIS/Photos/Camera Uploads. It is just below the comment CHANGE THE NEXT LINE. Replace /CHANGE/THIS/Photos/Camera Uploads with your upload folder. Save the file. If you would rather not edit a file, use way A or B: each writes this file for you.
- Start the helper. The first time, Docker downloads the image: the helper, packed for Docker.

```
docker compose up -d
```

- Ask the helper whether everything is right.

```
docker exec phlix-camera-upload python -m phlix_upload doctor
```

#### The Compose file, exactly as you download it

Change only the line under CHANGE THE NEXT LINE.

```
# Phlix Camera Upload
#
# This file starts the helper that receives the photos and videos the Phlix
# app uploads from your iPhone or iPad, and writes them into a folder of your
# Plex photo library.
#
# How to use this file:
#   1. Change the one line marked CHANGE THE NEXT LINE below.
#   2. In the folder that holds this file, run:  docker compose up -d
#   3. Open https://YOUR-SERVER:7459 in a browser to check that it runs.
#      The browser warns about the certificate. That is expected.
#
# If something does not work, ask the helper what is wrong:
#   docker exec phlix-camera-upload python -m phlix_upload doctor
#
# Setup guide: https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/
# If the app cannot find the helper:
#   https://github.com/jrl8085/phlix-camera-upload/blob/main/NETWORKING.md

services:
  phlix-camera-upload:
    image: ghcr.io/jrl8085/phlix-camera-upload:1
    container_name: phlix-camera-upload

    # Start again by itself when the server or Docker restarts.
    restart: unless-stopped

    # The Phlix app looks for the helper on port 7459 of your server.
    ports:
      - "7459:7459"

    volumes:
      # Your upload folder: the folder on this server where the photos go.
      #
      # It must be inside a folder that one of your Plex photo libraries
      # includes. If it is not, Plex never shows the photos.
      #
      # Make the folder before you start the helper. Docker refuses to start
      # the helper if the folder is missing. The helper writes files as the
      # user who owns the folder.
      #
      # Write the path as it is on the server itself. If Plex runs in Docker,
      # do not use the path from inside the Plex container.
      #
      # Examples:
      #   Linux      /mnt/media/Photos/Camera Uploads
      #   Synology   /volume1/photo/Camera Uploads
      #   TrueNAS    /mnt/tank/media/Photos/Camera Uploads
      #   Mac        /Users/you/Pictures/Camera Uploads
      #   Windows    C:\Users\you\Pictures\Camera Uploads
      #
      # Spaces in the path are fine. If the path has a "#" after a space, or
      # a ":" before a space, put the whole path in 'single quotes'.
      - type: bind
        # CHANGE THE NEXT LINE. Keep "source: " and write your folder after it.
        source: /CHANGE/THIS/Photos/Camera Uploads
        target: /photos
        bind:
          create_host_path: false

      # The helper's own data: the list of paired phones, the list of files
      # it has received, and its certificate. No photos are kept here.
      # Docker makes a folder named "config" next to this file. Keep it: if
      # it is lost, every phone has to pair again.
      # If your tool has no "next to this file" (TrueNAS, Portainer), write a
      # full path in place of ./config, for example:
      #   /mnt/tank/apps/phlix-camera-upload:/config
      - ./config:/config

    # Lets the helper find Plex Media Server on this machine.
    extra_hosts:
      - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"

    # The helper can never gain more rights than it was started with.
    security_opt:
      - "no-new-privileges:true"

    # Optional settings. The helper works without any of them.
    #
    # To use one, remove the "# " in front of "environment:" and in front of
    # the setting you want. Leave the other spaces as they are. Then run
    # "docker compose up -d" again.
    #
    # environment:
    #   # Where Plex Media Server is. Set this if the helper's status page
    #   # says "Plex Media Server: Not found", or to make sure that the helper
    #   # asks your own server and no other.
    #   PLEX_URL: "http://192.168.1.10:32400"
    #
    #   # Write files as this user and group. Without these, the helper uses
    #   # the owner of the upload folder.
    #   PUID: "1000"
    #   PGID: "1000"
    #
    #   # Permissions for new files and folders. With 022, other users may
    #   # read them. With 002, the group may also change them.
    #   UMASK: "022"
    #
    #   # The name that the app and the status page show for this helper.
    #   NAME: "Phlix Camera Upload"
    #
    #   # Who may pair. auto: the owner of the Plex server pairs without a
    #   # code and everyone else types the pairing code. code: everyone types
    #   # the code. plex: only the owner of the Plex server may pair.
    #   PAIRING: "auto"
    #
    #   # Your own pairing code, in place of the one the helper makes. Write
    #   # at least 6 letters or digits between the quotes.
    #   PAIRING_CODE: ""
    #
    #   # The folders the helper makes inside the upload folder. You can use
    #   # {device}, {year}, {month} and {day}.
    #   PATH_TEMPLATE: "{device}/{year}/{year}-{month}"
    #
    #   # Refuse uploads that would leave less than this many GB free. Uploads
    #   # that are still arriving count too.
    #   MIN_FREE_GB: "2"
    #
    #   # The largest single file the helper accepts, in GB.
    #   MAX_UPLOAD_GB: "50"
    #
    #   # More file types to accept, besides the usual photo and video types.
    #   # Separate them with commas.
    #   EXTRA_EXTENSIONS: "insp,lrv"
    #
    #   # How much the log says: debug, info, warning or error.
    #   LOG_LEVEL: "info"
    #
    #   # Write "off" only if your own reverse proxy adds HTTPS in front of
    #   # the helper. Phlix talks HTTPS only: with "off" and no such proxy,
    #   # the app cannot use the helper.
    #   TLS: "on"
    #
    #   # Your own certificate and its key, as paths inside the container.
    #   # Set both. A file you put in the config folder is at /config/...
    #   TLS_CERT: "/config/my-cert.pem"
    #   TLS_KEY: "/config/my-key.pem"
    #
    # PORT, BIND, UPLOAD_DIR and CONFIG_DIR exist too. With Docker you do not
    # need them. To use another port on your server, change only the first
    # number in the "ports" line above, for example "8443:7459". The app
    # looks for port 7459 by itself, so with another port you type the
    # helper's address into the app.
```

Prefer docker run? The README (https://github.com/jrl8085/phlix-camera-upload#the-same-with-docker-run) has the one command that does the same.

Done when doctor ends with Nothing needs fixing. Next: check that the helper runs (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#check).

#### Steps and notes for your system

On Unraid, Synology, TrueNAS SCALE and QNAP, follow these steps in place of ways A and C. The notes on Docker Desktop and on Plex in Docker add to the ways above.

#### Unraid

Unraid has no Docker Compose, so the one-command installer does not work here. Use the template (https://github.com/jrl8085/phlix-camera-upload/blob/main/unraid/phlix-camera-upload.xml) in place of the Compose file.
- Open the Unraid terminal.
- Make your upload folder inside a share that your Plex photo library includes, and give it to Unraid's standard user and group. Put your own path in place of the example. If the folder is there already, run only the second line.

```
mkdir "/mnt/user/Photos/Camera Uploads"
chown 99:100 "/mnt/user/Photos/Camera Uploads"
```

- Download the template:

```
wget -O /boot/config/plugins/dockerMan/templates-user/my-phlix-camera-upload.xml https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jrl8085/phlix-camera-upload/main/unraid/phlix-camera-upload.xml
```

- On the Docker tab choose Add Container, and pick phlix-camera-upload in the Template list.
- Set Photos to your upload folder and choose Apply.

The template runs the helper as Unraid's standard user and group (PUID 99, PGID 100). The chown command above lets that user write to the upload folder. To open the status page, choose WebUI on the container's icon. If the status page says "The helper cannot write here", run the chown command on the folder that you set as Photos, then reload the page. If Plex runs in a container, the upload folder must be inside a folder that the Plex container has.

Next: check that the helper runs (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#check).

#### Synology (Container Manager, DSM 7.2 or later)

Synology offers Container Manager only on some models, and only with DSM 7.2 or later. Synology lists the models under Applied Models on its Container Manager page (https://www.synology.com/en-global/dsm/packages/ContainerManager). If your model is not there, these steps do not work on your NAS. Run the helper on another computer at home instead, as in The helper is on a different machine than Plex, or on another port (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#net-other-machine).
- In File Station, make your upload folder inside the shared folder that your Plex photo library uses.
- In File Station, make a folder for the helper, for example docker/phlix-camera-upload.
- Open Container Manager, choose Project, then Create. Enter the name phlix-camera-upload and choose the folder from step 2 as the path.
- Choose Create docker-compose.yml as the source and paste the contents of docker-compose.yml (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/docker-compose.yml) (the full text, with a Copy button (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#compose-file)).
- Change the one line to your upload folder's full path, for example /volume1/photo/Camera Uploads. File Station shows the full path under Properties, as Location.
- Finish the wizard. Container Manager downloads the image and starts the helper.

If the DSM firewall is on, allow TCP port 7459 under Control Panel › Security › Firewall.

To run a command such as doctor, switch on SSH first: under Control Panel › Terminal & SNMP › Terminal, tick Enable SSH service and choose Apply. Then sign in with ssh NAME@SERVER, as a DSM user in the administrators group, and put sudo in front of the command. Switch SSH off again when you no longer need it.

To see the pairing code without SSH, open Container Manager, choose Container, select phlix-camera-upload, then choose Action › Details and open the Log tab. Search it for Pairing code.

If the status page says "The helper cannot write here", open Control Panel › Shared Folder › Edit › Permissions and give Read/Write permission to the user who owns the upload folder. Change this in DSM, not with chown or chmod: DSM manages access with its own rules.

Next: check that the helper runs (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#check).

#### TrueNAS SCALE (24.10 or later)

Do not use the one-command installer here: let TrueNAS manage the helper.
- Make your upload folder inside the dataset that your Plex photo library uses.
- Go to Apps › Discover Apps, open the menu with three dots, and choose Install via YAML.
- Enter the name phlix-camera-upload and paste the contents of docker-compose.yml (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/docker-compose.yml) (the full text, with a Copy button (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#compose-file)).
- Change the photos line to your upload folder's full path, for example /mnt/tank/media/Photos/Camera Uploads.
- Change ./config:/config to a full path, for example /mnt/tank/apps/phlix-camera-upload:/config, and choose Save.

To run a command, open System › Shell and put sudo in front of it.

Next: check that the helper runs (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#check).

#### QNAP (Container Station 3, QTS 5.1 or QuTS hero h5.1 or later)

Do not use the one-command installer here: let Container Station manage the helper.
- In App Center, install Container Station and open it.
- In File Station, make your upload folder inside the shared folder that your Plex photo library uses. Its full path starts with /share/ and the name of the shared folder, for example /share/Multimedia/Photos/Camera Uploads. If Plex shows your library's folder as /share/CACHEDEV1_DATA/Multimedia/Photos or similar, that is the same folder, and that path works too.
- In File Station, also make a folder for the helper's own data, for example phlix-camera-upload in the shared folder named Container. Its full path is then /share/Container/phlix-camera-upload.
- In Container Station, click the arrow next to Explore, at the top, and choose Create Application. Or go to Applications and choose Create.
- Enter the name phlix-camera-upload and paste the contents of docker-compose.yml (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/docker-compose.yml) (the full text, with a Copy button (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#compose-file)).
- Change the one line to your upload folder's full path. Change ./config:/config to the folder from step 3, for example /share/Container/phlix-camera-upload:/config. Both paths start with /share/.
- Choose Validate, then Create. Container Station downloads the image and starts the helper.

The helper writes files as the owner of the upload folder. On QNAP, the account named admin is the superuser, root. If you made the upload folder as admin, the files belong to admin, and doctor says "The helper runs as root". That is fine: Plex can still read them. To have the files belong to another user, make the upload folder while you are signed in to QTS as that user. The folder then usually belongs to that user, and so do the photos.

To run a command such as doctor, open Containers in Container Station, select phlix-camera-upload and choose Execute. Add the command without docker exec phlix-camera-upload in front, for example python -m phlix_upload doctor, and run it. The pairing code is also on the container's Logs tab: look for Pairing code:.
