Where this page says to change docker-compose.yml and run docker compose up -d, open Applications in Container Station instead. Select phlix-camera-upload, click the arrow next to Edit and choose Recreate. Change the text there and choose Update.

If QuFirewall is on and Phlix does not find the helper, open QuFirewall › Firewall Profiles and edit the profile in use. Choose Add Rule. Set Permission to Allow and Source to IP, with your home network's subnet, for example 192.168.1.0/24. Set Protocol to TCP and Port to 7459, and choose Apply. Put the rule above any rule that denies all, then choose Apply again and Yes.

Next: check that the helper runs (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#check).

#### A Mac or Windows PC with Docker Desktop

- On a Mac, all three ways work. On Windows, use way B or C: the one-command installer is for Linux and macOS.
- Plex runs on the Mac or PC itself, not in Docker. The helper still finds it.
- Write the photos line as a Mac or Windows path: /Users/you/Pictures/Camera Uploads or C:\Users\you\Pictures\Camera Uploads.
- If Docker says the folder is not shared, add it in Docker Desktop under Settings › Resources › File sharing.
- On Windows, set your home network to Private before you start the helper. Windows 11 makes a network Public when you first connect to it, and the answer below lets the phone in on a Private network only. Choose Private only for your own home network: it lets the other devices there find the PC.
  - Windows 11: open Settings › Network & internet, choose Wi-Fi and then the network you are connected to, or choose Ethernet. Under Network profile type, choose Private network.
  - Windows 10: open Settings › Network & Internet, choose Wi-Fi or Ethernet and then your network. Under Network profile, choose Private.

- When Windows asks about Docker Desktop Backend, usually the first time the helper starts, make sure that only the box for Private networks is ticked, and choose Allow access. Docker Desktop Backend is the part of Docker Desktop that takes the phone's connections.
- Windows keeps that answer. If you chose Cancel, closed the window, or allowed it on public networks only, the phone cannot reach the helper on your home network. To be asked again, open the Start menu, type Windows PowerShell, and choose Run as administrator. Run the command below. Then quit Docker Desktop, start it again, and answer as above.

```
Remove-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "Docker Desktop Backend"
```

- On a Mac, if macOS asks whether Docker may accept connections from your network, allow it.
- Uploads work only while Docker Desktop runs and the computer is awake. Switch on Settings › General › Start Docker Desktop when you sign in.
- On Windows, type the commands in PowerShell, and use curl.exe where this page says curl.

Then install with way A (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#install-one-command) (on a Mac), way B (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#install-with-ai) or way C (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#install-by-hand), above.

#### Plex itself runs in Docker

- Choose an upload folder that the Plex container can see: it must be inside one of the folders you gave the Plex container.
- In the helper's Compose file, write the folder's path as it is on the server, not as it is inside the Plex container. If Plex has /mnt/media:/data and shows your library's folder as /data/Photos, the helper's line is /mnt/media/Photos/Camera Uploads.
- The helper finds Plex on the server's port 32400 by itself. If its status page says "Plex Media Server: Not found", set PLEX_URL: see Networking help (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#net-plex-docker).

To see both paths side by side, run this in a terminal on the server, with the name of your Plex container in place of plex:

```
docker inspect --format '{{range .Mounts}}{{.Type}}  {{.Source}}  =>  {{.Destination}}{{println}}{{end}}' plex
```

Each line shows a path on the server on the left, and the same folder's path inside Plex on the right. Example: the line is bind /mnt/media => /data, and Plex shows /data/Photos. Your library's folder on the server is then /mnt/media/Photos, and your upload folder is /mnt/media/Photos/Camera Uploads.

To see the name of your Plex container, run:

```
docker ps --format '{{.Names}}  {{.Image}}'
```

Then go back to find your system (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#your-system).

### Finish Step 1: check that the helper runs

Open the helper's status page in a browser on another device on your home network. The iPhone you will connect is the best one for this: if the page opens in Safari there, the network between the two is fine. Replace SERVER with your server's address, for example https://192.168.1.10:7459.

```
https://SERVER:7459
```

Your server's address is four numbers with dots between them, such as 192.168.1.10. To find it:
- If you used way A, the installer printed it at the end, in the line that starts with Status page:.
- On Unraid you do not need it here: choose WebUI on the container's icon.
- On Linux, type hostname -I in the terminal. The address is usually the first one it prints.
- On a Mac, type ipconfig getifaddr en0 in Terminal. If it prints nothing, try en1 in place of en0.
- On Windows, type ipconfig in PowerShell and read the line IPv4 Address under Wi-Fi or Ethernet.
- If you open your NAS in a browser by a name on your home network, such as nas.local, the name works here too: https://nas.local:7459.

Your browser warns that the connection is not private. That is expected: choose Advanced or Show Details, then continue to the page. A home server has no public name that a certificate authority could vouch for, so the helper makes its own certificate, and browsers warn about every certificate made that way. Phlix does not rely on the browser's check: it remembers the helper's exact certificate when it pairs.

The page should say Upload folder: Ready and Plex Media Server: Found. If it says something else, run the doctor command on the server: it tells you what to do. On Synology, TrueNAS SCALE and QNAP, the steps for your system (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#platforms) say where to run it.

```
docker exec phlix-camera-upload python -m phlix_upload doctor
```

When all is well, it prints something like this:

```
Phlix Camera Upload 1.0.3
OK       The helper is running on port 7459
OK       The upload folder /photos can be written to.
OK       223.6 GB free on the upload disk.
OK       Plex Media Server found: its owner can pair from Phlix without a code.
OK       1 paired, 37 files stored (33.0 MB).
NOTE     Pairing code: run `python -m phlix_upload code` the same way to see it.
Nothing needs fixing.
```

When something needs fixing, a line that starts with PROBLEM is followed by a line that starts with Fix:.

If the page does not open at all:
- Check that the address starts with https://. The helper does not answer http://.
- Run the doctor command above on the server. If it says The helper is running on port 7459, the helper is running, and something stands between your device and the server: a firewall on the server, or a guest Wi-Fi. See Networking help (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#networking).
- If Docker says that the container is not running, read the log: docker logs phlix-camera-upload. See The helper does not start (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#ts-start).

One setting in Plex. In Plex, switch on Settings › Library › Scan my library automatically. Plex shows new files only after it scans. Phlix asks Plex for a scan once your photos have arrived, but only when your Plex account owns the server; the setting covers everyone else in your home, and is a second check for you. It depends on the server noticing new files, which typically fails for folders mounted over the network: for those, also switch on Scan my library periodically (Plex: Library settings (https://support.plex.tv/articles/200289526-library/)).

Step 1 is done when the status page says Upload folder: Ready and Plex Media Server: Found. If it says Not found, phones can still pair with the pairing code, and Networking help (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#net-plex-docker) says how to let the helper find Plex. Next: Step 2: Connect your iPhone (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#connect).

### Step 2: Connect your iPhone
- Connect your iPhone or iPad to your home Wi-Fi.
- Open Phlix and go to Settings › Camera Upload. If Settings has no Camera Upload row, update Phlix: yours is older than 1.0.21. The Version row in Settings shows the number.
- Tap Check for the Helper, then Check My Network. If iOS asks whether Phlix may find devices on your local network, allow it: without that, Phlix cannot reach anything in your home. Phlix looks for the helper at your Plex server's address. Nothing is switched on, and nothing is uploaded, until it is found.
- When Phlix says Helper found, choose a folder name for this device, such as "Anna's iPhone", and tap Connect. If this device was connected to this helper before, leave the name as Phlix shows it: the device keeps its folder. With another name, its new photos go into a folder of that name.
- If Phlix now shows Enter the pairing code, type the helper's pairing code and tap Pair. Family members with their own Plex account see this step. If you own the Plex server and see it too, Phlix could not pair through Plex this time; the code works just as well, and the helper's status page usually says why, next to Plex Media Server. To see the code, run this on the server (Pairing: who needs a code (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#pairing), below, has the other ways):

```
docker exec phlix-camera-upload python -m phlix_upload code
```

- Phlix says Connected. Choose what to back up, Everything on this device or Only new photos, and tap Turn On Camera Upload.
- iOS asks whether Phlix may read your photos. Choose Full Access, so that it can back up all of them.

A green dot and "Connected to" the helper's name (Phlix Camera Upload, unless you set NAME) mean the connection is good. Grey means you are away from home, where Phlix waits. Orange means something needs your attention, and the screen says what.

#### Pairing: who needs a code
- You own the Plex server. Phlix pairs without a code, as long as the helper's status page says Plex Media Server: Found. The app shows the helper a short-lived token from your Plex server, the helper asks Plex whether it belongs to the server's owner, and then forgets it.
- Everyone else, such as family members with their own Plex account, types the helper's pairing code. The owner of the server finds it with this command, or in the helper's log each time it starts:

```
docker exec phlix-camera-upload python -m phlix_upload code
```
 Capital letters, spaces and the dash do not matter. On Synology and QNAP, the container's log shows the code without a terminal: see the Synology steps (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#sys-synology) or the QNAP steps (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#sys-qnap).

If Phlix says Helper not found, Camera Upload stays off, and nothing is sent anywhere. Read The app does not find the helper (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#ts-not-found).

Step 2 is done when the Camera Upload screen shows a green dot and "Connected to" the helper's name. To watch the first photos arrive, reload the helper's status page: Files stored goes up. They land in this device's folder inside your upload folder (see Where your photos go (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#where)), and show in Plex once it has scanned (One setting in Plex (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#plex-scan)). Next: What happens next (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#after).

### What happens next
- With Phlix open, uploads start straight away and run as fast as your Wi-Fi allows. While the Camera Upload screen is open and uploading, the phone does not lock by itself, so a first big backup is quickest with the phone on its charger and that screen open.
- With Phlix closed, iOS lets it carry on in short bursts, mostly while the phone charges. That is how iOS treats every app, and it means a large library takes a few days in the background. New photos follow by themselves.
- Away from home, Phlix does not start uploads or look for your server, apart from rare cases that the privacy policy (https://phlixapp.com/privacy/#camera-upload) lists; even then, your photos go only to your own helper. Backing up carries on when the phone is back on your home Wi-Fi.
- When everything is backed up, the screen says so with a green tick. Switch on Notify Me When Backed Up to get a notification as well.

The Camera Upload screen always shows where you stand: how many photos are backed up out of how many, what is uploading now, what was backed up recently, and how many items cannot be backed up. Those are items that Photos holds no file for, that are larger than your server accepts, or that keep disappearing from your server.

#### What is uploaded
- The photos and videos in your own Photo Library. Videos are optional (Include Videos).
- Screenshots and screen recordings are left out unless you switch on Include Screenshots.
- Each photo is uploaded as it looks in Photos at that moment. An edited photo uploads edited. A Live Photo uploads as its still photo.
- With iCloud Photos and "Optimize iPhone Storage", iOS fetches the full-size original from iCloud when Phlix asks for it.
- Not uploaded: hidden photos, shared albums and photos synced from a computer.
- Photos that Phlix 1.0.21 or later saves from Plex to Photos are not uploaded by the phone or tablet that saved them: they came from your server, so they count as backed up without the helper being asked. Phlix keeps the list of them in the app, on that device. Photos saved by an earlier version of Phlix, or before you deleted Phlix and installed it again, are not on the list, and are uploaded like any other photo.

### Where your photos go

Each phone or tablet has its own folder inside the upload folder. Inside it there is one folder for each year and one for each month:

```
Camera Uploads/
  Anna's iPhone/
    2026/
      2026-11/
        IMG_1234.HEIC
        IMG_1235.MOV
  Ben's iPad/
    2026/
      2026-10/
```

- The year and month come from the photo's own date. The file keeps its name from the phone, and its modification time is set to the photo's date.
- Two different photos with the same name are both kept: the second becomes IMG_1234 (2).HEIC. Nothing is ever overwritten.
- The same photo from two phones is stored once.
- With helper 1.0.2 or later (see Update the helper (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#update-helper)), a photo counts as backed up only while its file is in the upload folder. If you delete a file, or a device's whole folder, and the photo is still on the device, Phlix uploads it again. Phlix asks the helper which files are there each time you open the Camera Upload screen, every half minute while that screen is open, at once when you tap Check Connection, and from time to time while it backs up at home. After you connect a device again, nothing that device uploaded counts as backed up until the helper has confirmed it: the screen says Checking… for a moment, then shows the count.
- To keep a photo off the server, hide it in the Photos app: Phlix never uploads hidden photos.
- To change the layout, set PATH_TEMPLATE. See All the settings (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#settings).

#### If you, or a program, move files on the server

- Sort files into any folders inside the upload folder, keeping their names: Phlix finds them there. A device's folder you rename is followed, and new photos go into it. A file you rename, or move out of the upload folder, is uploaded again. A file you edit still counts.
- If a program on the server moves new files away, set it to leave the folders in place. A file that keeps leaving the upload folder soon after each upload is sent again three times at most, then listed under Can't Be Backed Up. A photo whose folder you deleted is never listed there: Phlix sends it again each time (helper 1.0.3 or later). So if the program also removes the folders it empties, the three-times limit never applies, and Phlix uploads the same photos again each time it backs up. When you connect the phone again, or delete the folder that held a listed photo, Phlix sends that photo again too.
- A recycle bin is not the upload folder. If your upload folder is a whole drive on Windows, a folder you delete goes to that drive's $RECYCLE.BIN. Helper 1.0.3 or later never counts a photo there as backed up; helper 1.0.2 could.

### Troubleshooting

Start with the helper's own check:

```
docker exec phlix-camera-upload python -m phlix_upload doctor
```

If it says that the container is not running, read the log instead: docker logs phlix-camera-upload. On Synology, TrueNAS SCALE and QNAP, the steps for your system (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#platforms) say where to run these. In Phlix, the Camera Upload screen names the problem it sees, and Check Connection tries again.

Or go straight to your problem:
- What the Camera Upload screen says (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#ts-screen)
- The app does not find the helper (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#ts-not-found)
- Photos do not appear in Plex (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#ts-plex)
- Pairing does not work (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#ts-pairing)
- Files are owned by the wrong user, or the helper cannot write (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#ts-permissions)
- The helper does not start (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#ts-start)
- Networking help (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#networking): another machine or port, firewalls, guest Wi-Fi, VPNs, "not on your home network"
- Update, change or remove the helper (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#changing): updates, the upload folder, settings, paired devices

#### What the Camera Upload screen says

| Phlix says | What to do |
| "Paused: not on your home network" | That is normal away from home. At home, check that the phone is on your Wi-Fi. If it is, see Phlix says "Paused: not on your home network", but I am at home (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#net-home). |
| "Can't reach the helper" | - If Phlix also says "iOS is keeping Phlix off your local network", see the iPhone's own settings (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#net-ios). If not, the phone is on your home network and the helper does not answer. - Open https://SERVER:7459 in a browser, or run doctor, to see whether the helper is running. Then tap Check Connection. - If the helper is running and Phlix still cannot reach it, see Networking help (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#networking). If you moved the helper to another port or another machine, see The helper is on a different machine than Plex, or on another port (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#net-other-machine). |
| "Your server's disk is too full" | Free some space on the upload disk, or lower MIN_FREE_GB (see All the settings (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#settings)). Backing up carries on by itself. The disk has too little room for the next file: the helper always keeps some space free, 2 GB unless you changed MIN_FREE_GB. |
| "The helper can't write to its folder" | See Files are owned by the wrong user, or the helper cannot write (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#ts-permissions). |
| "The helper no longer knows this device" | See Pairing does not work (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#ts-pairing). |
| "The server's identity has changed" | See Pairing does not work (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#ts-pairing). |
| "Some uploads didn't go through" | Phlix tries them again by itself. Tap Check Connection to try now. |
| "Your helper needs an update" | Update the helper (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#update-helper). The one on your server is older than 1.0.2: it cannot tell Phlix which photos it still has, so a photo deleted on the server would keep counting as backed up. The Helper Version row, under Server on the Camera Upload screen, shows which version is running. |
| "This device is almost out of space" | Free some space on the phone. Phlix makes a copy of each file on the phone before it sends it: it needs about 300 MB free, and more for a long video, room for a copy of the whole file. |

#### The app does not find the helper

| Cause | Fix |
| The helper is not installed yet. | Install it first, on the machine that runs Plex Media Server: Step 1: Install the helper (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#install). Then tap Check Again in Phlix. |
| The helper is not running. | Open https://SERVER:7459 in a browser. If the page does not open, run docker compose ps in the helper's folder (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#changing), then read the log with docker logs phlix-camera-upload. |
| The phone is not on your home network. It may be on mobile data, a guest Wi-Fi or a VPN. | Connect the phone to the same network as the server. See Networking help (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#networking). |
| iOS is keeping Phlix off your local network. | On the iPhone, open Settings › Apps › Phlix and switch on Local Network. |
| A firewall on the server blocks the port. | Allow TCP port 7459 (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#net-firewall) from your home network. |
| The helper is on another address or port than Plex. | In Phlix, type its address into the field under Helper not found, for example 192.168.1.10:7459, and tap Check This Address. |
| Phlix is older than 1.0.21. Settings then has no Camera Upload row. | Update Phlix to 1.0.21 or later. The Version row in Phlix's Settings shows what you have. |

#### Photos do not appear in Plex

First find out whether the files arrive: the status page shows Files stored, and you can look in the upload folder.

| Cause | Fix |
| The files arrive, and Plex has not scanned yet. | In Plex, switch on Settings › Library › Scan my library automatically. If the upload folder is on a network share, Plex may not notice new files by itself: also switch on Scan my library periodically (Plex: Library settings (https://support.plex.tv/articles/200289526-library/)). To scan now, open the photo library's menu and choose Scan Library Files. |
| The files arrive, and the upload folder is not inside a folder of a Plex photo library. | In Plex, add the upload folder to your photo library: Edit Library, then Add folders. Or choose another upload folder, change the line in docker-compose.yml, and run docker compose up -d. |
| The files arrive, and Plex runs in Docker without that folder. | Choose an upload folder inside a folder that the Plex container has. |
| No files arrive. | Open Phlix on your home Wi-Fi and look at Settings › Camera Upload. It says what it is waiting for. After the first 100 uploads, the rest need Phlix Pro. |
| Files arrive only while Phlix is open. | Check that Background App Refresh is on for Phlix in the iPhone's Settings: if it is off, uploads wait until you open Phlix. Even with it on, iOS decides when a closed app may run: never the moment the phone joins your Wi-Fi, and mostly while the phone charges. |
| The status page says "too little: uploads are paused". | Free some space on the disk, or lower MIN_FREE_GB. Backing up carries on by itself. |

#### Pairing does not work

| Phlix says | Fix |
| "That pairing code isn't right." | Print the code again: docker exec phlix-camera-upload python -m phlix_upload code. |
| "Too many wrong tries." | Wait a few minutes and try again: the helper slows down guessing. |
| "Your Plex account doesn't own this server." | Ask the owner for the helper's pairing code. That is the normal way for family members. |
| "The helper couldn't confirm with Plex that this is your server." | Enter the pairing code instead. To pair without a code, make sure the status page says "Plex Media Server: Found"; if not, set PLEX_URL. |
| "The server's identity has changed" | The helper was reinstalled without its old config folder, so it has a new certificate and no record of what it received. On every phone that was paired: - Note the name next to Folder on the Camera Upload screen: the name of this device's folder inside your upload folder on the server. - Choose Disconnect, connect again, and type that same folder name. Phlix sends this device's photos again. With the same folder name, a file that is still where the helper put it is recognized by its content and is not stored twice. With another folder name, the photos are stored a second time. If you did not reinstall the helper, something else is answering at that address, and Phlix has sent it nothing. |
| "The helper no longer knows this device" | In Phlix, choose Disconnect, then connect again. Photos already on the server stay there, and nothing is uploaded twice. The pairing of this device has ended on the server, and Phlix has switched Camera Upload off. That happens when someone removes the device with the unpair command, or when the same device pairs again, for example after a phone was restored or set up again. |
| "This helper only pairs with the owner of its Plex server." | The helper's PAIRING setting is plex, so it takes no pairing code, and only the owner of the Plex server can pair. Sign in to Phlix with the Plex account that owns the server. The helper must also have found Plex. Its status page must say "Plex Media Server: Found". If it does not, set PLEX_URL. To let other people pair with a code, set PAIRING to auto. |

#### Files are owned by the wrong user, or the helper cannot write

| Cause | Fix |
| The helper writes files as the owner of the upload folder. If root owns that folder, the files belong to root. | Set PUID and PGID to the user and group you want, then run docker compose up -d. The command id USERNAME prints a user's numbers. |
| The status page says "The helper cannot write here". | Change the upload folder's owner or permissions, or set PUID and PGID. On Unraid, run chown 99:100 on the upload folder in the Unraid terminal. On Synology, give the folder's owner Read/Write permission under Control Panel › Shared Folder › Edit › Permissions. After a change to the folder, reload the status page: it checks again each time. |
| The log says "it cannot use its own data folder". | The user that the helper runs as may not write to its config folder. The log line names that user by number. In the helper's folder, run sudo chown -R USER:GROUP config with those numbers, or set PUID and PGID, then docker compose up -d. |
| Fedora, RHEL or Rocky Linux with SELinux: the same message, or "The helper cannot write here". | Label both folders for containers, in the helper's folder: sudo chcon -R -t container_file_t "/your/upload/folder" config, then docker compose restart. |

#### The helper does not start

| Docker or the log says | Fix |
| "bind source path does not exist" | The upload folder in docker-compose.yml does not exist, or the line still says /CHANGE/THIS. Make the folder, check the path, and run docker compose up -d again. |
| "bind source path does not exist", and the folder is there, or "operation not permitted" | Docker may have come as a Snap, which Ubuntu Server offers while it installs. To check, run snap list docker. If it lists docker, that Docker cannot start the helper. It sees only some of your folders, and it cannot start a container with the helper's setting no-new-privileges. Replace it. First remove the Snap with sudo snap remove docker. That deletes everything this Docker holds: its containers, images and volumes. Your upload folder and the helper's folder stay. If other programs run in this Docker, such as Plex, make sure that you can set them up again before you remove it. Then install Docker with Docker's own instructions (https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/), and run docker compose up -d again. |
| "Nothing is mounted at /photos" | Start it with the Compose file as it is. The container was started without its folders, and the helper refuses to start then, so that uploads can never land inside the container and be lost. |
| The helper does not start; its log says the upload folder is empty | It stored photos there before, so it waits for a share or disk that is not mounted yet, and starts by itself once it is. If you emptied the folder on purpose, make a folder named .phlix-upload-tmp in it. On Unraid, start the container again on the Docker tab. |
| "permission denied" from Docker itself | Put sudo in front of each docker command. |
| "port is already allocated", "address already in use" or "Ports are not available" | Give the helper another port: Docker cannot use port 7459 on the server, usually because another program or another container uses it. In docker-compose.yml, change only the first number in the ports: line, for example to "7460:7459", and run docker compose up -d again. If you used way A, run the installer again with the new port instead, and answer y when it asks whether to replace the Compose file: curl -fsSL https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/install.sh | sh -s -- --port 7460. Phlix looks for port 7459 by itself, so type the helper's address with the new port into Phlix, for example 192.168.1.10:7460. See The helper is on a different machine than Plex, or on another port (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#net-other-machine). |

### Networking help

Most homes need nothing from this section: the helper runs on the machine that runs Plex, the phone is on the same Wi-Fi, and Phlix finds it. Read on if your network is less ordinary, or if Phlix says Helper not found.

#### First, test from the iPhone

On the iPhone, open Safari and go to https://SERVER:7459, with your server's address. Tap through the certificate warning.
- The status page opens. The network is fine. In Phlix, type the same address into the field under Helper not found and tap Check This Address. If Phlix still cannot reach it, check the iPhone's own settings (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#net-ios).
- The page does not open. The phone cannot reach the helper. Find your situation below.

#### How Phlix finds the helper

Phlix asks nothing of your network except one thing: it must be able to open a connection from the phone to TCP port 7459 on the server. There is no broadcast, no discovery protocol and no cloud relay. Phlix takes the local addresses of the Plex server you are signed in to, tries port 7459 on each, and accepts only an answer from the real helper. If your helper is somewhere else, you type its address once.

The helper's networking guide on GitHub (https://github.com/jrl8085/phlix-camera-upload/blob/main/NETWORKING.md) goes further: for each way to set up the network, it says when to use it, which lines to change in docker-compose.yml and what to type into Phlix, with complete examples for nginx and Caddy.

#### The helper is on a different machine than Plex, or on another port

In Phlix, type the helper's address into the field under Helper not found, for example 192.168.1.20, or 192.168.1.20:8443 for another port, and tap Check This Address. Before a search, tap Enter the Helper's Address to open the field.

On another machine, two more things matter:
- The upload folder must still be inside your Plex photo library. Usually that means a network share that both machines mount. The helper writes files as the owner of the folder, or as PUID and PGID. Plex may not notice new files on a share by itself. In Plex, also switch on Settings › Library › Scan my library periodically (Plex: Library settings (https://support.plex.tv/articles/200289526-library/)).
- Set PLEX_URL to your Plex server's address, for example http://192.168.1.10:32400, so that the server's owner can pair without a code. Without it, everyone pairs with the pairing code, which works just as well.

To use another port on the same machine, change only the first number in the ports: line of the Compose file, for example "8443:7459".

A phone that is already paired does not find the helper at a new port, or on another machine than Plex, by itself. It says Can't reach the helper. On that phone, choose Disconnect, tap Check for the Helper, then Enter the Helper's Address, type the new address and tap Check This Address. If the helper still has its config folder, leave the folder name as Phlix shows it: the phone keeps its folder, and nothing is uploaded twice. Phlix asks again what to back up, with the choices you made before already set.

#### Plex runs in Docker, and the helper says "Plex Media Server: Not found"

Phones can still pair with the pairing code. Only pairing without a code needs the helper to reach Plex.

The helper looks for Plex on port 32400 at the Docker host, at the container's gateway, at 127.0.0.1 and at a container named plex. That covers Plex on the server itself, Plex in Docker with host networking, and Plex in Docker with port 32400 published. If yours is elsewhere, tell the helper. In docker-compose.yml, remove the #  in front of environment: and PLEX_URL, write your Plex server's address, and run docker compose up -d:

```
    environment:
      PLEX_URL: "http://192.168.1.10:32400"
```

If port 32400 of Plex is not published on the server, the server's address does not answer either. The networking guide on GitHub (https://github.com/jrl8085/phlix-camera-upload/blob/main/NETWORKING.md) shows how to put the helper on the Docker network of Plex. Look there for "Plex in a container on its own Docker network".

If Plex runs in Docker with bridge networking and Phlix does not find the helper by itself, Plex is reporting its address inside Docker instead of the server's own. Type the server's address into Phlix once.

#### A firewall on the server

Allow TCP port 7459 from your home network, and from nowhere else.
- ufw (Ubuntu, Debian): sudo ufw allow from 192.168.1.0/24 to any port 7459 proto tcp, with your own network range.
- firewalld (Fedora, RHEL, Rocky): sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --add-port=7459/tcp, then sudo firewall-cmd --reload.
- Synology: Control Panel › Security › Firewall.
- QNAP: if QuFirewall is on, allow TCP port 7459 from your home network in the profile in use, under QuFirewall › Firewall Profiles. The QNAP steps (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#sys-qnap) say how.
- Windows: set your home network to Private, and allow Docker Desktop Backend on private networks only. The note for Mac and Windows (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#sys-desktop) shows how, and what to do if you chose Cancel.
- macOS: allow Docker when macOS asks whether it may accept incoming connections.

The firewall can also keep the helper away from Plex on the same machine. The status page then says "Plex Media Server: Not found". The helper asks Plex from its own Docker network, not from your home network. So a rule for your home network does not let it in, and PLEX_URL does not change that. Pair with the pairing code, which works just as well. Or let the helper's Docker network reach port 32400, and nothing else. This command shows the network's range:

```
docker network inspect --format '{{range .IPAM.Config}}{{.Subnet}} {{end}}' phlix-camera-upload_default
```

The network is named after the helper's folder. If Docker says that there is no such network, write your folder's name in place of phlix-camera-upload. Then allow that range. With ufw, put it in place of RANGE: sudo ufw allow from RANGE to any port 32400 proto tcp. On Synology, add a rule under Control Panel › Security › Firewall › Edit Rules: ports Custom, TCP 32400, source IP Specific IP with that range, action Allow. Drag it above any rule that denies. After docker compose down, Docker may give the helper another range, so check it again then.

#### Guest Wi-Fi, "client isolation", or a separate network for phones or smart devices (VLANs)

Guest networks and routers with "AP isolation" or "client isolation" keep devices from talking to each other. That is their job, and it stops the phone from reaching the server.
- The simple fix: put the phone on the same network as the server.
- If you keep phones and servers on separate networks on purpose, add one rule in your router or firewall: allow the phones' network to reach the server's address on TCP port 7459. Phlix needs nothing else, and no discovery traffic has to cross between the networks. Then type the server's address into Phlix.

Mesh Wi-Fi, several access points and a server on a cable are all fine, as long as they are one network.

#### Phlix says "Paused: not on your home network", but I am at home

In Phlix, open Settings › Camera Upload and tap This Is My Home Network. Phlix adds the network you are on, but only if your helper answers from it, with the certificate it had when you paired. A network where your helper does not answer is never added.

Why it happens: Phlix knows your home by the address range of the Wi-Fi network your phone was on when you paired, for example 192.168.1.0/24. It never reads the Wi-Fi's name and needs no location permission. If you changed your router, moved to another network at home, or have two networks, the range no longer matches.

A new router usually gives the server a new address as well. Phlix then says "The helper didn't answer". In that case choose Disconnect, then connect again, as in Connect your iPhone (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#connect). Leave the folder name as Phlix shows it: the phone keeps its folder, and nothing is uploaded twice.

#### The iPhone's own settings: Local Network, VPNs

- Local Network. iOS asks once whether Phlix may find devices on your local network. If the answer was no, Phlix cannot reach anything at home. Open the iPhone's Settings › Apps › Phlix (or Privacy & Security › Local Network) and switch on Local Network. Phlix tells you when this is the reason.
- VPN apps. Many VPN apps block the local network while they are on. Look for a setting named "Allow LAN access" or "Local network sharing", or pause the VPN at home. iCloud Private Relay does not get in the way.
- Mobile data. Phlix never uploads over mobile data. Low Data Mode on your home Wi-Fi does not hold uploads back: they stay on your own network.

#### My server's address changes

Give the server a fixed address: in your router, look for "DHCP reservation" or "static lease" and reserve the address the server has now. That helps Plex as much as the helper.

If the address does change, Phlix looks for the helper again at your Plex server's new address by itself, and carries on once it finds the same helper there. You can also disconnect and connect again; nothing is uploaded twice.

#### Away from home: remote access, VPNs into your home, port forwarding

Camera Upload is made for your home network, on purpose. Phlix checks the Wi-Fi network the phone is on, so a VPN into your home from somewhere else does not start uploads, and neither does Plex Remote Access.

One case looks different. Phlix knows your home by its address range, and a network somewhere else can use the same range: many routers use 192.168.1.x. Phlix takes such a network for home and tries your helper's address. No server there shows your helper's certificate, so no photo is sent. While the phone is on that network, the Camera Upload screen says "Can't reach the helper". The cause is that network, not your helper at home. Backing up carries on when the phone is back on your home Wi-Fi.

Do not forward port 7459 to the internet. It would add nothing, because Phlix only uploads at home, and it would expose a service on your server to everyone.

#### A reverse proxy, your own domain name, or your own certificate

You do not need any of these. If you already run them at home and prefer a name such as https://uploads.home.example:
- Your own certificate: put the certificate and its key in the helper's config folder. Set TLS_CERT and TLS_KEY to their paths inside the container, where that folder is /config: for example /config/my-cert.pem and /config/my-key.pem. In Phlix, type the name with the helper's port: https://uploads.home.example:7459. With a certificate that iOS already trusts, Phlix uses iOS's own check, so a renewed certificate needs no new pairing.
- A reverse proxy (Nginx Proxy Manager, Traefik, Caddy): set TLS: "off" on the helper and let the proxy add HTTPS. Phlix connects only over HTTPS. Lift the proxy's upload size limit and switch off request buffering, or large videos fail: in Nginx, client_max_body_size 0; and proxy_request_buffering off;.
- With a reverse proxy, type its full address in Phlix: https://uploads.home.example.
- Keep it inside your home. Do not route uploads through a cloud proxy: it would see your photos, and most limit uploads to 100 MB.

The home-network rule stays the same: Phlix uploads only on your home Wi-Fi, whatever the address.

#### Docker network modes: host, macvlan, Unraid's br0

- Bridge with a published port is what the Compose file uses, and what works everywhere.
- Host networking works too: replace the ports: and extra_hosts: lines with network_mode: host.
- macvlan, ipvlan or Unraid's br0 give the helper its own address on your network. Type that address into Phlix. A container on such a network usually cannot reach the server it runs on, so set PLEX_URL to an address it can reach, or pair with the pairing code.
- Docker inside WSL 2 without Docker Desktop: Windows does not pass connections from your network into WSL by default. Use Docker Desktop, or WSL's mirrored networking mode.

The helper uses IPv4. A home network with only IPv6 is not supported yet.

Still stuck? Write to support (https://phlixapp.com/support/) and paste what doctor printed. It holds no passwords and no file names.

### Update, change or remove the helper

The helper has no settings screen. Everything is one file, docker-compose.yml, and one command to apply it: docker compose up -d, in the helper's folder.

The helper's folder is the folder that holds docker-compose.yml. If you used way A, it is phlix-camera-upload in your home folder: type cd ~/phlix-camera-upload to go there. If an AI assistant installed the helper (way B), its last message names the folder. If you used way C, it is the folder you made in its step 2.

On QNAP, the QNAP steps (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#sys-qnap) say how to make these changes in Container Station.

#### Update the helper

```
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d
```

Run both in the helper's folder. Phones stay paired: the helper keeps its data in the config folder, and an update does not touch it. On Unraid, use Check for Updates on the Docker tab. In Phlix, the Helper Version row on the Camera Upload screen shows which version is running, and the screen says Your helper needs an update for a helper older than 1.0.2. What changed in each version is on the releases page on GitHub (https://github.com/jrl8085/phlix-camera-upload/releases).

#### Move the upload folder

Stop the helper with docker compose down, move the folder on the server, change the source: line in docker-compose.yml, and run docker compose up -d. Phones stay paired, and nothing is uploaded twice. Remember that the new place must be inside a Plex photo library too.

#### The name of a device's folder

Phlix shows the folder in use on the Camera Upload screen, next to Folder. To rename it, rename the folder on the server: the helper finds it there and puts new photos in it. Or choose Disconnect, connect again and type a new name: new photos go into a folder of that name, and photos already on the server stay where they are.

#### All the settings

In docker-compose.yml, remove the #  in front of environment: and in front of the setting you want, then run docker compose up -d.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| PLEX_URL | found automatically | The address of Plex Media Server, such as http://192.168.1.10:32400. |
| PAIRING | auto | auto: the Plex server's owner pairs without a code, everyone else types the code. code: everyone types the code. plex: only the owner may pair. |
| PAIRING_CODE | made by the helper | Your own pairing code, at least 6 letters or digits. |
| NAME | Phlix Camera Upload | The name that Phlix and the status page show for this helper. |
| PATH_TEMPLATE | {device}/{year}/{year}-{month} | The folders made inside the upload folder. You can use {device}, {year}, {month} and {day}. |
| PUID, PGID | owner of the upload folder | The user and group that files are written as. |
| UMASK | 022 | Permissions for new files. With 002, the group may also change them. |
| MIN_FREE_GB | 2 | The helper refuses uploads that would leave less free space than this. |
| MAX_UPLOAD_GB | 50 | The largest single file the helper accepts. |
| EXTRA_EXTENSIONS | none | More file types to accept, besides the usual photo and video types. |
| TLS, TLS_CERT, TLS_KEY | on, own certificate | For a reverse proxy or your own certificate. See A reverse proxy, your own domain name, or your own certificate (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#net-proxy). |

The README (https://github.com/jrl8085/phlix-camera-upload#settings) describes each one in full.

#### See or remove paired devices

```
docker exec phlix-camera-upload python -m phlix_upload devices
```

To stop one device from uploading, for example a phone you sold:

```
docker exec phlix-camera-upload python -m phlix_upload unpair "Anna's iPhone"
```

To make every unpaired person need a new code, change the pairing code, then restart the helper. Until it restarts, the old code still works and the new one does not. Phones that are already paired stay paired.

```
docker exec phlix-camera-upload python -m phlix_upload new-code
docker restart phlix-camera-upload
```

If you set PAIRING_CODE yourself, change the code there instead, and run docker compose up -d.

#### Remove the helper

```
docker compose down
```

Removing the helper never deletes photos. Everything it received stays in your upload folder. To remove the helper's own data as well, delete the folder you made for it. In Phlix, switch Camera Upload off or choose Disconnect.

### Questions

#### Is Camera Upload a beta?

Yes. Camera Upload is a beta in Phlix 1.0.21 or later. It does what the list on this page (https://phlixapp.com/camera-upload/#beta) says. Keep your own backup of anything you cannot replace, and tell us what goes wrong: in Phlix, open Settings and tap Send Feedback, or use the support page (https://phlixapp.com/support/).

#### What happened to Plex's own Camera Upload?

Plex announced in March 2021 that it was ending support for its Camera Upload, with removal targeted for June 2021. Camera Upload in Phlix is a separate feature of an independent app: it copies your photos into a folder of your Plex photo library through the helper on your own server. The whole story, with Plex's announcement (https://phlixapp.com/plex-camera-upload/).

#### Does it delete photos from my iPhone?

No. Phlix copies your photos and videos to your server. It never deletes or changes anything in your Photo Library. Freeing space on the phone stays your decision.

#### Does it work away from home, or over mobile data?

No, on purpose. Phlix uploads only while the phone is on your home Wi-Fi. Away from home it does not start uploads or look for your server, apart from rare cases that the privacy policy (https://phlixapp.com/privacy/#camera-upload) lists; even then, your photos go only to your own helper. Photos you take on a trip upload when you are back.

#### Do I need Plex Pass?

No. The helper writes ordinary files into a folder of your Plex photo library, and that works with every Plex Media Server. The photos then show in your Plex photo library, and in Phlix.

#### What does it cost?

The helper for your server is free. In the app, the first 100 uploads are free, so you can see it work from end to end. Phlix Pro (https://phlixapp.com/#pricing) uploads the rest, and what you take from then on.

#### Can the whole family use it?

Yes. Each iPhone and iPad pairs by itself and gets its own folder. The owner of the Plex server pairs without a code; everyone else types the helper's pairing code. If two phones hold the same photo, the server stores it once.

#### How long does the first backup take?

With Phlix open on the Camera Upload screen and the phone on its charger, it runs as fast as your Wi-Fi allows. With Phlix closed, iOS gives it short bursts, mostly while the phone charges, so a large library takes a few days. Either way you can see the count rise in the app.

#### Is this a sync? What if I delete a photo?

It is a one-way copy, from the phone to the server. Deleting a photo on the phone leaves the copy on the server, and nothing comes back to the phone. If you delete a file on the server and the photo is still on the phone, Phlix uploads it again.

#### Does it work with iCloud Photos?

Yes. Phlix reads the photos in your Photo Library, wherever iOS keeps them. With "Optimize iPhone Storage", iOS downloads the full-size original from iCloud when Phlix asks for it, and Phlix needs about 300 MB free on the phone to get each file ready. Shared albums are not included.

#### Is there an Android version?

No. Phlix is an app for iPhone and iPad.

### Privacy and security
- Your photos stay on your network. The phone sends them straight to your server. Phlix, the developer, never receives them and cannot reach them. The helper contacts nothing on the internet; the only thing it calls is your own Plex Media Server.
- The connection is encrypted. When a phone pairs, Phlix remembers the helper's exact certificate. From then on it talks only to a server that shows it.
- Pairing needs proof. The owner of the Plex server proves it through Plex, and the helper never stores a Plex token. Everyone else needs the pairing code, and the helper slows down anyone who guesses.
- A paired phone can only add. The helper offers no way to list, read, download, overwrite or delete a stored file. It accepts photo and video files only.
- You can read the code. The helper's source is public on GitHub (https://github.com/jrl8085/phlix-camera-upload), with the security notes (https://github.com/jrl8085/phlix-camera-upload/blob/main/SECURITY.md).

The privacy policy (https://phlixapp.com/privacy/#camera-upload) has the full description.

- GitHub repository: Source code, README, Unraid template, the skill. (https://github.com/jrl8085/phlix-camera-upload)
- README: All the instructions in one document. (https://github.com/jrl8085/phlix-camera-upload/blob/main/README.md)
- Networking guide: Each way to set up the network, with examples. (https://github.com/jrl8085/phlix-camera-upload/blob/main/NETWORKING.md)
- Security notes: How the helper is built to be safe, and how to report a security problem. (https://github.com/jrl8085/phlix-camera-upload/blob/main/SECURITY.md)
- Releases: What changed in each version of the helper. (https://github.com/jrl8085/phlix-camera-upload/releases)
- Docker image: ghcr.io/jrl8085/phlix-camera-upload:1, for Intel, AMD and Arm. The page also lists unknown/unknown. That is not an image: it is the record of how the image was built and what is in it. (https://github.com/jrl8085/phlix-camera-upload/pkgs/container/phlix-camera-upload)
- Unraid template: The file that adds the helper on Unraid's Docker tab. (https://github.com/jrl8085/phlix-camera-upload/blob/main/unraid/phlix-camera-upload.xml)
- Issues: Problems reported with the helper, and a place to report one. For a security problem, read the security notes first. (https://github.com/jrl8085/phlix-camera-upload/issues)

#### On this site

- Support: Answers to common questions, and a form to write to us. (https://phlixapp.com/support/)
- Privacy policy: Camera Upload (Beta): What Camera Upload stores and sends, and to whom. (https://phlixapp.com/privacy/#camera-upload)

#### Phlix: your Plex photos, the way they deserve

Camera Upload (Beta) backs up your camera roll to your own server, on your home Wi-Fi only. Phlix also saves any photo from your server to the Photos app, and shows your whole library on a date timeline, with slideshows on your TV. Download Phlix Free (https://apps.apple.com/app/phlix-photos/id6796820208?ppid=ac65ec1b-2558-4773-9352-ad5f5355c4b8)

iPhone and iPad · iOS 17 or later
Camera Upload needs Phlix 1.0.21 or later.
